definition.stemRaw:
You are evaluating a customer-support agent’s configuration. Each prospective tool belongs to one of four categories: (1) required to carry out defined tasks, (2) frequently used and reduces hand-offs, (3) occasionally helpful for unrelated work, (4) speculative future utility.  
  
Which categories should generally stay in the agent configuration?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Only category 3, because occasionally useful tools for unrelated work provide broader coverage and should take priority over tools required for the agent’s defined tasks.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Only category 4, because speculative future-utility tools provide the most flexibility and should be configured even when no defined task currently requires them.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Categories 1 and 2 only, because they map to defined tasks and the agent’s regular hand-offs.

choices.label: D
choices.text: All four categories, because broader tool access is categorically better for agent performance regardless of whether the tools map to defined tasks or regular hand-offs.

definition.explanation:
Agent tools should be limited to capabilities that support defined tasks and regular operational workflows. Required tools enable the agent’s intended work, and frequently used tools that reduce hand-offs improve its routine execution. Occasionally useful unrelated tools and speculative future tools do not justify current access and unnecessarily broaden the available tool set. OpenAI’s API supports constraining a model to a predefined set of allowed tools.

**Learn more:** [OpenAI API Reference — Responses tool configuration](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/responses-streaming/response/custom_tool_call_input/delta?lang=javascript)

definition.stemRaw:
A technical team is cataloguing risks particular to Claude’s use in a document-grounded Q&A system.  
  
Which two items are failure modes inherent to LLM-based systems rather than generic software defects? (Select two.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: An expired TLS certificate blocks outbound API calls to Claude.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A database connection timeout causes retrieval to return an empty result set.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The model refuses a legitimate query because surface features trigger an overly broad safety pattern.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A misconfigured load balancer routes requests to a deprecated API version.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The model generates a plausible-sounding answer unsupported by any retrieved document.

definition.explanation:
Safety mechanisms can decline a legitimate request when a classifier identifies features associated with a restricted category; Anthropic notes that benign work can trigger some refusal categories. LLMs can also hallucinate, producing content that is factually incorrect or inconsistent with the supplied context, so a plausible answer may lack support in the retrieved documents. Expired certificates, retrieval timeouts, and incorrect load-balancer routing are ordinary infrastructure or configuration defects.

**Learn more:** [Refusals and fallback - Claude Platform Docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/refusals-and-fallback) · [Reduce hallucinations - Claude Platform Docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/test-and-evaluate/strengthen-guardrails/reduce-hallucinations)

definition.stemRaw:
You are adding human review to a high-volume classification pipeline in which reviewing every output is impractical.  
  
Which sampling strategy best balances throughput and quality oversight?

choices.label: A
choices.text: No sampling, relying entirely on user complaints to reveal quality and safety problems after they affect users.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Risk-stratified sampling that reviews all low-confidence and high-impact outputs and a smaller random sample of high-confidence routine outputs.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Inverse sampling that reviews only high-confidence routine outputs and skips low-confidence and high-impact outputs.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Universal review of every output regardless of confidence or throughput impact.

definition.explanation: Risk-stratified sampling directs human review toward outputs with the greatest likelihood or cost of error—low-confidence and high-impact cases—while random sampling of routine high-confidence outputs provides an ongoing check for hidden quality issues. This preserves scalable throughput without abandoning oversight.

definition.stemRaw:
You operate an interactive assistant where per-turn latency is the primary performance constraint. Quality on routine turns is already acceptable.  
  
Which configuration change most directly improves latency without disproportionately harming quality?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Disable prompt caching entirely to ensure fresh context processing on every request, preventing stale prefix content from affecting latency-sensitive interactions.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Reduce retrieval depth to the top-k passages that historically cover the answer, and cache stable system-prompt content.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increase retrieval depth to the corpus maximum to improve recall regardless of latency.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Switch every turn to the heaviest available model to maximize output quality, accepting that the increased model latency will worsen the per-turn SLO rather than improve it.

definition.explanation:
Retrieving only the top-k passages that historically supply the needed information reduces retrieval work and the prompt context processed on each turn, while preserving routine-answer quality. Caching stable system-prompt content avoids reprocessing an unchanged prefix. Retrieval adds compute and round trips, and preserving cached context improves cache utilization.

**Learn more:** [Retrieval augmented generation (RAG) and indexes in Microsoft Foundry](https://learn.microsoft.com/th-th/azure/foundry/concepts/retrieval-augmented-generation) · [OpenAI API Reference — Realtime server events](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/realtime-server-events/conversation/item/done)

definition.stemRaw:
You are evaluating patterns for a batch document-classification job with fixed stages: extract metadata, classify, summarize, and persist.  
  
Which pattern is the best fit, and why?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A workflow pattern, because agentic patterns do not support tool invocations and therefore cannot execute the persist step that writes results to the downstream store.

choices.label: B
choices.text: An agentic pattern, because the open-ended planning capability of agents produces more consistent structured outputs than a fixed workflow graph on classification tasks.

choices.label: C
choices.text: An agentic pattern, because agents are categorically more accurate than workflows and therefore always preferable regardless of step predictability.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A workflow pattern, because the steps are well-defined and predictable per-request token cost is preferred over flexibility.

definition.explanation: A workflow pattern fits a deterministic batch process whose stages are known in advance. It provides repeatable orchestration and predictable per-request token costs, whereas agentic flexibility and open-ended planning are unnecessary for this fixed sequence.

definition.stemRaw:
A pilot AI assistant for procurement specialists has an 89 percent first-response acceptance rate, but follow-up surveys show that specialists often override the assistant’s vendor recommendations after considering criteria the assistant did not assess. The pilot owner wants to launch the assistant unchanged because of the strong acceptance rate.  
  
Which two Discernment-competency observations should you raise **BEFORE** approving the launch? *(Select two.)*

choices.label: A
choices.text: The acceptance rate alone proves readiness for general production use.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The survey response rate may not be statistically representative of all specialists.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The unconsidered criteria represent a scope gap in the assistant’s input space.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Acceptance does not establish whether recommendations remain correct after specialist review.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The pilot duration was probably too short to demonstrate reliability across the full year.

definition.explanation: Specialists’ overrides after considering omitted vendor-selection criteria reveal that the assistant’s evaluated input space is incomplete. A high initial acceptance rate measures early user uptake, not whether recommendations remain correct after the fuller specialist review needed for a procurement decision.

definition.stemRaw:
You are a solution architect building a Claude-based assistant that has access to 60 internal tools across multiple business domains. Loading every tool definition with each request increases token usage and time to first response.  
  
Which design pattern best resolves this issue without reducing capability breadth?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Apply progressive tool discovery so a curated initial subset is exposed and additional tools are loaded on demand based on the task.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Use a separate model call to summarize all 60 tool definitions before each user turn.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increase the maximum context length and load all 60 tool definitions on every request, accepting the higher token cost and latency as necessary for full capability.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Hard-code a fixed set of five tools per request to reduce token usage, regardless of whether those tools are relevant to the current task.

definition.explanation:
Progressive tool discovery keeps the full tool catalog available while deferring nonessential tool definitions until they are relevant to the task. This lowers initial context-token usage and time to first response without limiting the assistant to a permanently fixed subset of tools. Anthropic documents deferred tool loading with tool search specifically for large tool sets so that only relevant tools are presented for a query.

**Learn more:** [MCP connector — Claude Platform Docs](https://docs.anthropic.com/ja/docs/agents-and-tools/mcp-connector)

definition.stemRaw:
You are investigating an MCP server that fails on its initial launch but works on later runs. System permission dialogs appeared during that first launch.  
  
Which response is the most appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Recognize the first-run permission grant as the cause, document the expected behavior in onboarding guidance, and confirm that subsequent runs succeed.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Reinstall the operating system to clear all permission state without first confirming whether the one-time permission grant caused the failure.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Disable operating-system permission dialogs entirely, accept the resulting security implications, and proceed without confirming whether the failure recurs.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Treat the first-run failure as a permanent fault, replace the MCP server, and do not verify whether subsequent runs succeed.

definition.explanation: A first-run operating-system permission grant can temporarily block startup until the user authorizes the required access. If later launches succeed, the appropriate response is to confirm that behavior and document the expected authorization step for onboarding rather than treating it as a permanent failure.

definition.stemRaw:
An engineering organization is rolling out Claude Code across 200 developers. A team lead proposes that AI-generated pull requests bypass the standard code-review process for changes under 50 lines, because small changes are viewed as low risk and review capacity is limited.  
  
Which two Diligence-competency objections should you raise? Each correct answer presents part of the solution. (Select two.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Removing review eliminates the verification mechanism required for AI-generated output across the workflow.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Code-review capacity should be expanded to handle every code change submitted across the team.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The threshold should be increased to 200 lines to capture more changes.

choices.label: D
choices.text: AI-generated pull requests should be rejected by default across the organization.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Line count is a poor proxy for the actual risk introduced by a code change.

definition.explanation:
AI-generated changes still require verification before integration; Anthropic’s security guidance assigns users responsibility for reviewing proposed code and advises reviewing all suggested changes before approval. Line count does not represent the security, correctness, authorization, configuration, dependency, or operational impact of a change, so it cannot safely determine whether review may be bypassed. Automated review can supplement, but does not replace, existing manual code-review and security practices.

**Learn more:** [Claude Code Security](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/security) · [Automated Security Reviews in Claude Code](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11932705-automated-security-reviews-in-claude-code)

definition.stemRaw:
You are choosing a model for a new production workload and must complete the upstream steps before empirically testing candidate models.  
  
Which two steps must be completed **BEFORE** testing a representative sample on a candidate model? Each correct answer is part of the solution. (Select two.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Select the lightest model that consistently meets the quality bar across the sample.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Retest the model choice when a new model version becomes available.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Choose a candidate model based on the requirements profile and known capabilities.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Define the quality bar, latency tolerance, and expected volume for the workload.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sign off the production rollout plan with the platform and security teams.

definition.explanation:
A candidate model should be selected using the workload’s defined requirements—required output quality, latency tolerance, and expected volume—together with known model capabilities. A representative evaluation is performed after those criteria and an initial candidate are established. Selecting the lightest model that passes the evaluation, retesting new versions, and obtaining rollout approval are subsequent activities.

**Learn more:** [Model selection | OpenAI API](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/model-selection) · [API deployment checklist | OpenAI API](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/deployment-checklist)

definition.stemRaw:
You are developing a test strategy for a Claude-based pipeline that processes sensitive financial data.  
  
Which two testing types should be prioritized to address both safety under attack and correctness across components? (Select two.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Adversarial tests using prompt-injection and malformed-input cases.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Regression tests against a stable reference set of previously known-good outputs.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Smoke tests that verify core paths after each deployment.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Integration tests that verify end-to-end pipeline behavior across all components.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Unit tests targeting only individual prompt-template rendering logic.

definition.explanation:
Adversarial testing validates resistance to hostile inputs such as prompt injections and malformed data, helping protect sensitive information and prevent unsafe behavior. End-to-end integration testing verifies that the pipeline’s components interact and behave correctly as a complete system; together, these tests cover both attack resilience and cross-component correctness.

**Learn more:** [Mitigate jailbreaks and prompt injections](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/test-and-evaluate/strengthen-guardrails/mitigate-jailbreaks) · [Prompting best practices](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-prompting-best-practices)

definition.stemRaw:
You are evaluating model-selection claims used by a peer team.  
  
For each of the following statements, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.text: Heavier-reasoning models typically consume more of the rate limit and run more slowly than lighter models on the same input.
A representative-sample evaluation on the target workload is the right basis for confirming a model selection.
The most capable model is always the right choice regardless of the workload profile.
Tiered routing can serve routine traffic with a lighter model while reserving a heavier model for traffic that needs its capability.
Selecting a model based on which version was most recently announced is the right basis for production decisions.

definition.explanation:
Higher reasoning effort trades increased latency and token use for deeper reasoning, so it can consume more rate-limit capacity. Model selection should be confirmed through evaluations that represent the production workload and its quality, latency, and cost requirements. The most capable model is not invariably appropriate: smaller models can be better for cost-sensitive or latency-sensitive routine work. Tiered routing appropriately directs simple requests to a lighter model and reserves a stronger model for complex requests. Announcement recency does not establish production suitability; measured performance on the target workload does.

**Learn more:** [Model guidance](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/latest-model?model=gpt-5.5) · [Models](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models)

definition.stemRaw:
You are assessing instrumentation in a multi-agent system.  
  
Which two findings represent valid observability gaps in the instrumentation? Each correct answer provides a complete solution. (Select two.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Trace spans for each agent step are exported to the shared distributed-tracing backend.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Latency and token usage on every span are emitted to the central metrics pipeline.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Tool-call payloads and outcomes are recorded with redaction applied to known sensitive fields.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Model identity and version on each turn are not recorded with the turn artifacts.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Request-scoped correlation identifiers do not propagate across agent and tool calls.

definition.explanation:
Model identity and version must be captured with each turn so behavior, latency, token usage, failures, and regressions can be attributed to the specific model configuration. Request-scoped correlation identifiers must propagate across agent and tool calls so their spans and telemetry remain connected within one distributed trace. OpenTelemetry defines GenAI model attributes and explains that context propagation enables correlation across distributed service boundaries.

**Learn more:** [OpenTelemetry GenAI attributes](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/registry/attributes/gen-ai/) · [OpenTelemetry context propagation](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/concepts/context-propagation/)

definition.stemRaw:
An engineer accidentally commits an API key to the repository by placing it in `.claude/settings.json`.  
  
Which configuration design principle was breached?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Project-scope configuration should always override user-scope configuration.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Managed configuration must be applied before project-scope configuration is read.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Credentials must be resolved at runtime from a secret store and never stored in version-controlled files.

choices.label: D
choices.text: MCP server definitions must reside in environment variables to prevent scope conflicts.

definition.explanation:
API keys are credentials and must not be committed to version-controlled configuration files, where repository access and history can expose them. They should be supplied securely at runtime, such as through a secret store or protected environment-based mechanism. Anthropic documents using a key helper that retrieves a key from a Vault secret for dynamic credentials.

**Learn more:** [LLM gateway configuration — Anthropic](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code/llm-gateway)

definition.stemRaw:
A document-analysis service handles legal filings that average 80,000 tokens each. Attorneys query every filing an average of 14 times during a case. The current architecture sends the entire filing with every query. The CFO has asked you to lower per-query costs while maintaining response quality. The security officer requires that filing content not be stored outside Fabrikam's tenancy.  
  
Which optimization approach should you recommend?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Summarize each filing once at intake and run all subsequent queries against the summary.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cache the filing as the prompt prefix for reuse across the 14 queries per case.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Index filings in a vector store and retrieve only the relevant passages per query.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Move the workload to a smaller Claude model to reduce the per-token cost paid.

definition.explanation:
Prompt-prefix caching reuses the processed representation of the unchanged filing across the repeated queries, reducing input-token cost and latency while preserving the full-document context and response quality. Azure OpenAI prompt caching is designed for identical long prefixes, does not alter the response content, and does not share prompt caches between Azure subscriptions.

**Learn more:** [Prompt caching with Azure OpenAI in Microsoft Foundry Models](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/openai/how-to/prompt-caching)

definition.stemRaw:
You are creating an ethics-review checklist for AI-supported deployments.  
  
Which two checks should be included on the list? Each correct answer provides a complete solution. (Select two.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Confirm that vendor licensing terms permit the planned production use of the model.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Verify that outputs do not rely on generalizations about people that the underlying data does not support.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Confirm that high-impact decisions retain human accountability rather than being attributed to the model.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Restrict ethics review to outputs that exceed a defined model-confidence threshold.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Confirm that latency and throughput targets are met across supported user populations.

definition.explanation:
Ethical AI deployment requires fairness in how people are represented and treated, so outputs should not make unsupported generalizations about people. It also requires clear human accountability: people and deploying organizations remain responsible for consequential decisions and must retain appropriate oversight rather than assigning responsibility to a model.

**Learn more:** [What is Responsible AI? - Azure Machine Learning](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/machine-learning/concept-responsible-ai) · [Guidance for integration and responsible use with conversational language understanding](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/responsible-ai/clu/clu-guidance-integration-responsible-use)

definition.stemRaw:
You are classifying chunking strategies by the corpus type to which each is best suited.  
  
For each chunking strategy, select the applicable corpus type: “Long Structured Documents,” “Heterogeneous Short Records,” or “Code or Hierarchical Specs.”

blanks.label: function-level or section-level chunking for code modules
tree-aware chunking that follows code or specification hierarchy
per-record chunking where each record is one chunk
semantic chunking along clause or paragraph boundaries
fixed-size chunking with overlap for short records of similar length
hierarchical chunking that mirrors document section structure

definition.explanation: Function-level and tree-aware boundaries preserve the logical hierarchy of source code and specifications. Per-record and fixed-size overlapping chunks suit short, independently meaningful records. Semantic paragraph/clause boundaries and document-section hierarchies preserve the context and structure of long documents.

definition.stemRaw:
You are choosing a pattern for a compliance Q&A assistant that must respond to policy questions with citations from the authoritative internal source set. Latency, cost, and audit predictability are priorities.  
  
Which pattern is the best fit?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Augmented LLM with retrieval-augmented generation over the indexed authoritative corpus and citation rendering on each answer.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Multi-agent orchestration with a planner, researcher, and writer agent for every query.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A pure agent loop with open web-browsing tools to surface the most current policy information, without constraining retrieval to the authoritative internal corpus.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A static prompt with the entire policy corpus concatenated into every request.

definition.explanation: Retrieval-augmented generation retrieves relevant material from the indexed authoritative policy corpus for each response, enabling source-grounded citations and predictable auditability. It is typically more efficient and controlled than multi-agent orchestration, unrestricted web retrieval, or including the entire corpus in every prompt.

definition.stemRaw: For each statement, select Yes if it reflects a sound architectural practice. Otherwise, select No.

statements.text: Authentication and authorization run before retrieval so retrieval can filter by identity.
An asynchronous queue absorbs bursty traffic between intake and the model invocation layer.
Tax computation is encoded directly in the system prompt rather than in code.
Conversation logs include unredacted government identifiers to maximize signal for tuning.

definition.explanation:
Authorization before retrieval enables identity-based access filtering. Queues smooth burst traffic and decouple request intake from asynchronous model processing. Tax calculations require deterministic, testable application logic rather than prompt behavior. Government identifiers are sensitive PII, so logs should redact or mask them and restrict their use.

**Learn more:** [AWS Well-Architected Framework — Fail fast and limit queues](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/2023-10-03/framework/rel_mitigate_interaction_failure_fail_fast.html) · [Amazon Bedrock — Remove PII from conversations by using sensitive information filters](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/guardrails-sensitive-filters.html)

definition.stemRaw:
You are building an evaluation pipeline for a Claude-based deployment and must finish the specification steps before running the deployment against the dataset.  
  
Which two steps must be completed BEFORE running the deployment against the evaluation dataset? Each correct answer represents part of the solution. (Select two.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Publish the aggregated metrics to a dashboard and gate releases on threshold checks.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Curate and label the evaluation dataset to match the defined slices.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Review failure cases with subject matter experts to refine the scoring rubric.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Define the metrics and slices the framework will report across representative, edge, and adversarial cases.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Score the deployment outputs against the reference labels and aggregate the metrics.

definition.explanation:
Evaluation requires predefined, measurable success criteria and an evaluation set that reflects the intended task distribution, including edge cases. Metrics and slices establish what will be measured, while curated reference labels enable the resulting outputs to be scored. Aggregating scores, reviewing failures, and publishing dashboard results occur after the deployment has been run on that dataset.

**Learn more:** [Define success criteria and build evaluations — Claude Platform Docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/test-and-evaluate/develop-tests)

definition.stemRaw:
A managed agent deployment for claims triage has expanded from 6 tools to 34 tools over 18 months as product teams added capabilities. Triage accuracy has declined from 91 percent to 78 percent, and average tool-selection latency has risen by 2.3 seconds. A junior engineer has proposed placing a tool-router agent in front of the existing agent to filter the tool list for each request.  
  
Which two findings should you present to support capability decomposition before adding the router? Each correct answer represents part of the solution. (Select two.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Tool descriptions overlap across multiple claim categories within the agent’s tool set.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Several tools have not been invoked across the most recent 90 days of traffic.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The 34 tools serve four distinct claim-workflow domains within the triage scope.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The router pattern is well documented across publicly available agent literature.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The proposed router introduces an additional model call on every incoming request.

definition.explanation:
Four distinct claim-workflow domains provide clear capability boundaries for splitting the broad triage responsibility into focused agents with smaller, domain-specific tool sets. Adding a router introduces another model invocation for every request, which compounds latency rather than addressing the underlying overload created by a single agent selecting among dozens of tools. Microsoft’s agent guidance notes that tool selection degrades as agents accumulate many tools and that each delegated agent invocation adds latency.

**Learn more:** [Agents as Tools — Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/agent-framework/journey/agents-as-tools) · [Multi-agent — OpenAI API documentation](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/responses-multi-agent)

definition.stemRaw:
An architect is assessing a Claude-based candidate-screening tool before deployment. A stakeholder claims that no bias evaluation is needed because the model was not trained on company data.  
  
Which two responses most accurately dispute this claim? (Select two.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Transparency obligations are satisfied by disclosing that an AI system is in use, without further evaluation.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fairness testing is required only when the training dataset is known to contain protected-class labels.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The model may carry demographic biases from pretraining that manifest in screening outcomes regardless of fine-tuning.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The system should be evaluated on outcome-disparity metrics across protected groups before deployment.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Bias evaluation is unnecessary when the model provider has published a responsible-use policy.

definition.explanation:
A model can retain demographic biases from its broad pretraining even when it has not been trained on an organization’s data. For an employment-screening use case, fairness evaluation should measure whether outcomes differ across protected groups before deployment. NIST guidance calls for evaluating fairness and bias and using context-specific metrics to assess performance and harms across groups.

**Learn more:** [NIST AI RMF Core — Measure](https://airc.nist.gov/airmf-resources/airmf/5-sec-core/) · [NIST AI RMF Playbook — Measure](https://airc.nist.gov/airmf-resources/playbook/measure/)

definition.stemRaw:
You are ordering decomposed components in an invoice-processing pipeline.  
  
For every decomposed component, choose the execution layer to which it belongs: “Pre-Processing”, “Model Stage”, or “Post-Processing”.

blanks.label: Claude-based classification of invoice type
persistence of validated records to the system of record
schema validation of the extracted fields
Claude-based extraction of structured invoice fields
PII redaction on extracted text prior to model invocation
optical character recognition on scanned invoice images

definition.explanation: Pre-processing prepares invoice inputs for inference, including OCR and redacting sensitive text before model invocation. The model stage performs the Claude classification and structured-data extraction. Post-processing validates extracted output against its schema and persists only validated records to the system of record.

definition.stemRaw:
You are creating a prompt for a ticket-triage classifier with thirty clearly defined categories and clear descriptions of each category in the prompt.  
  
Which technique is the most appropriate starting point?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A chain-of-thought prompt for a routing decision that does not require multi-step reasoning.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A zero-shot prompt that specifies the categories with their descriptions and the required output format.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A prompt that demands the model invent new categories when the supplied ones do not fit.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A prompt with no category descriptions, expecting the model to infer the category set.

definition.explanation: For classification against a fixed taxonomy, a zero-shot prompt should state the allowed categories, define them clearly, and specify the required response format. This grounds the model in the intended label set and produces consistent, machine-readable routing decisions.

definition.stemRaw:
You are evaluating a Claude-based system whose primary risk is undetected quality drift in safety-relevant outputs after a model-version upgrade.  
  
Which assessment activity most directly mitigates this risk?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Disable adversarial evaluation entirely during model-version upgrade cycles to reduce evaluation cost, accepting that safety drift will go undetected until it appears in production.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Rotate adversarial inputs randomly so no two upgrades are scored on the same set.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Skip evaluation on each model-version upgrade and rely on user-submitted complaints to surface safety drift after the upgraded model has already served production traffic.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Maintain an adversarial evaluation set with version-attributed scoring so each upgrade is measured against the same set before promotion.

definition.explanation:
A stable adversarial evaluation set, scored and recorded by model version before promotion, provides a controlled regression comparison that can reveal safety-quality drift introduced by an upgrade. Anthropic recommends thoroughly testing applications with newer models before migrating to them.

**Learn more:** [Anthropic Claude Platform Docs — Model deprecations](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/about-claude/model-deprecations)

definition.stemRaw:
You are conducting a risk assessment for a planned Claude-based deployment and must finish the inventory steps before evaluating threats against assets.  
  
Which two actions must be completed **before** assessing threats against assets to estimate likelihood and impact? Each correct answer represents part of the solution. *(Select two.)*

choices.label: A
choices.text: Document the assessment outcome with risks, mitigations, residual risk, and acceptance owners.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Recommend mitigations and residual-risk acceptance for the risks that remain after analysis.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Identify the assets that the deployment touches, along with the sensitivity of each asset.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Recommend mitigations and residual-risk acceptance for risks that remain.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Enumerate the threat actors and attack vectors relevant to the deployment.

definition.explanation:
Risk likelihood and impact can be estimated only after identifying the assets affected by the deployment and their sensitivity, then identifying the relevant threat actors and attack vectors. Asset sensitivity establishes the potential consequence of compromise, while threat actors and vectors define the plausible threat scenarios. Mitigation recommendations, residual-risk acceptance, and outcome documentation follow the analysis.

**Learn more:** [Assess risks - AWS Well-Architected Responsible AI Lens](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/responsible-ai-lens/raibr03.html) · [Key security concepts for agentic AI on AWS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/agentic-ai-security/concepts.html)

definition.stemRaw:
Following an update to a prompt template, several test cases that had previously passed now generate unexpected outputs.  
  
Which test type is specifically intended to identify this kind of failure?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Integration tests that validate cross-component pipeline behavior.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Adversarial tests that probe for prompt-injection vulnerabilities.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Regression tests scored against a stable reference set of known-good behavior.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Smoke tests that confirm high-level system availability after the change.

definition.explanation: Regression tests detect unintended changes in previously correct behavior by evaluating the updated system against stable, known-good reference cases.

definition.stemRaw:
A platform team runs a self-hosted, multi-agent system on Kubernetes that coordinates seven specialized agents for invoice processing. The team uses approximately 40 percent of its engineering capacity for infrastructure maintenance, message-bus reliability, and agent-state recovery. The CFO has asked for an evaluation of a move to managed agent infrastructure to recover engineering capacity. The security officer requires all customer financial data to stay within an approved network boundary.  
  
Which factor should carry the greatest weight in your recommendation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Whether the current seven agents map cleanly to the patterns supported by managed agents.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Whether managed agents reduce per-invoice token costs across the existing processing volume.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Whether managed agents support the current bus topology used by the platform team.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Whether managed agent data handling satisfies the network boundary required by security.

definition.explanation: Compliance with the approved network boundary for customer financial data is a mandatory security constraint. Operational benefits such as reduced maintenance effort, lower token costs, or architectural compatibility cannot justify adopting a managed service that fails to meet that data-handling requirement.

definition.stemRaw:
You are determining where human review must remain in a proposed automated pipeline.  
  
Which placement represents sound human-in-the-loop design?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Place a human reviewer only after the irreversible action has already executed, making the review a post-hoc audit rather than a meaningful pre-action check or approval gate.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Place a human reviewer between the model’s output and any high-impact, irreversible action, with explicit criteria for what the reviewer must check before approval.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Place a human reviewer in the loop for a randomly selected sample of requests, without defining criteria for what the reviewer should check or which output categories require mandatory review.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Remove all human review steps from the pipeline to maximize throughput, accepting that high-impact and irreversible actions will be taken without any human approval or oversight.

definition.explanation: Human review should occur after the model produces its output but before any high-impact, irreversible action, and reviewers need explicit approval criteria. This preserves meaningful oversight and enables intervention before harm or irreversible consequences occur.

definition.stemRaw:
A Claude architect at a health services organization is establishing evaluation metrics for a clinical-summary pipeline. The pipeline must stay within a per-query cost ceiling and must never expose patient data to unauthorized roles.  
  
Which two metrics directly address these requirements? (Select two.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: BLEU score computed against a human-annotated reference summary set

choices.label: B
choices.text: Role-based access-control enforcement rate measured on a red-team dataset

choices.label: C
choices.text: Throughput measured as successful requests processed per minute

choices.label: D
choices.text: Per-query token cost measured against the defined cost ceiling

choices.label: E
choices.text: Response latency at the 95th percentile across a one-week sample window

definition.explanation:
Per-query token cost directly tests compliance with the defined cost ceiling. An RBAC enforcement rate measured on adversarial test cases directly tests whether authorization controls prevent unauthorized roles from accessing patient data. Claude API costs are driven by token usage, and RBAC assigns permissions to authorized users or groups.

**Learn more:** [Anthropic Pricing](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/about-claude/pricing?4810b549_page=3&73cdfb14_page=2&939688b5_page=1&e768fcd2_page=2) · [Implement role-based access control in applications](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/howto-implement-rbac-for-apps)

definition.stemRaw:
A Claude-based research assistant starts generating responses that confidently contradict its retrieved source documents, even though the retrieval pipeline has not changed.  
  
Which two diagnostic actions most directly identify the root cause of this behavior? (Select two.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Increase the context-window size to allow more retrieved chunks per query.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Switch the retrieval index to a denser embedding model to improve chunk-relevance scores.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Determine whether the failure reproduces on the previous model version to test for a model mismatch.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reduce the temperature setting to lower response variance across all query types.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Inspect the system-prompt grounding instructions to determine whether citation constraints remain intact.

definition.explanation:
Reproducing the behavior with the previous model version can isolate a model-version or model-routing mismatch when retrieval has remained unchanged. Reviewing the system prompt verifies that the instructions requiring answers to be grounded in retrieved content and constrained by citations have not been removed or weakened. Claude model updates can change instruction-following behavior, so Anthropic recommends testing applications when changing models.

**Learn more:** [Prompting best practices — Claude Platform Docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-prompting-best-practices) · [Model deprecations — Claude Platform Docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/model-deprecations)

definition.stemRaw:
You are assessing prompting claims in a peer’s design document.  
  
For each of the following statements, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.text: Zero-shot is appropriate as a starting point for closed-set classification when categories and descriptions are provided in the prompt.
Adding a few-shot example set with exact field names anchors output formatting on extraction tasks.
Chain-of-thought should be the default on every task regardless of complexity.
Leading-question framing is best mitigated by asking for an even-handed comparison with stated criteria.
Behavioral differences across model versions can be ignored once a prompt has been validated on one version.

definition.explanation: Zero-shot classification works when labels and their definitions are clearly specified. Few-shot examples with exact schema fields reinforce the desired extraction format. Chain-of-thought should be applied only when useful for the task, not as a blanket default. Neutral comparisons with explicit criteria counter leading framing. Model behavior can vary by version, so prompts require validation after version changes.

definition.stemRaw:
You are designing a content-moderation classifier that handles high volumes of user-generated comments under a tight per-message latency budget and uses well-defined classification labels.  
  
Which model selection best fits this workload?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Opus, because every moderation decision requires maximum reasoning depth regardless of classification complexity.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Haiku, because its latency and cost profile align with high-volume classification workloads that require limited reasoning depth.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Sonnet, because larger general-purpose models are preferred even when workload latency requirements are strict.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sonnet with extended thinking enabled, because deeper reasoning should be applied to every moderation request to improve edge-case handling.

definition.explanation:
Claude Haiku is designed for high-volume, latency-sensitive work such as classification, extraction, and routing. Its faster, lower-cost profile suits well-defined moderation labels that do not require deep reasoning, whereas larger models or added thinking increase latency without being necessary for this workload.

**Learn more:** [Anthropic Claude pricing and model guidance](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing)

definition.stemRaw:
A revenue-projection assistant is 38 percent above its monthly cost target. Profiling identifies three contributors: a 6,000-token policy preamble repeated on every call (45 percent of cost), retrieval of historical sales chunks averaging 3,000 tokens per call (30 percent), and inference on a flagship-tier model (25 percent). Stakeholders require that projection accuracy remain unchanged.  
  
Which two optimizations should you sequence first to reduce cost without affecting accuracy? Each correct answer represents part of the solution. (Select two.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Reduce the number of historical sales chunks retrieved across each query run.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Truncate the policy preamble to remove non-essential clauses from the prompt.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Enable prompt caching on the static policy preamble across the recurring calls.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Switch the workload to a smaller, faster Claude model tier across all queries.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Cache common retrieved sales chunks accessed across many of the daily queries.

definition.explanation:
Prompt caching lets recurring requests reuse an identical stable prefix, such as a policy preamble or frequently reused context, at a much lower input-processing cost while preserving the exact content supplied to the model. Caching the static policy and commonly reused historical-sales chunks therefore reduces the two largest repeatable prompt-related costs without changing the projection inputs or model tier.

**Learn more:** [Prompt caching — Claude Platform Docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching) · [Pricing — Claude API Docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing)

definition.stemRaw:
You are assessing retrieval-strategy claims used by a peer team.  
  
For each claim, select **Yes** when it is generally accurate; otherwise, select **No**.

statements.text: Dense vector retrieval is well suited to recovering paraphrased intent against unstructured text.
Sparse term-matching retrieval recovers exact terms (such as identifiers and rare tokens) more reliably than dense alone.
Structured query retrieval is the right fit for filter-and-aggregate workloads against a relational store with schema and indexes.
Hybrid retrieval is identical to dense-only retrieval and shares the same recall characteristics.
Random sampling of a data store is a sound retrieval strategy for production Q&A.

definition.explanation: Dense vector search captures semantic similarity, which supports paraphrase retrieval. Sparse lexical retrieval is strongest for exact strings, identifiers, and rare terms. Relational queries and indexes support deterministic filtering and aggregation. Hybrid retrieval combines sparse and dense approaches, giving it different retrieval and recall behavior from dense-only search. Random sampling provides no relevance guarantee, so it is not suitable for production question-answering retrieval.

definition.stemRaw:
An operations engineer says that a Claude-based pipeline started returning malformed JSON responses after a scheduled maintenance window, resulting in downstream processing failures.  
  
Which two investigative actions most directly isolate the root cause? (Select two.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Clear the prompt cache and resubmit all pending requests to eliminate stale cached prefixes.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Compare the current system prompt and output schema configuration against the last known good version from before the maintenance window.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Switch to a different Claude model tier to rule out provider-side changes as a contributing factor.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increase the max_tokens limit to determine whether output truncation is causing incomplete JSON structures.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Replay a set of premaintenance requests against the current configuration and inspect the raw model output before downstream parsing.

definition.explanation:
A configuration comparison can reveal whether maintenance altered the system instructions or output-schema requirements that govern JSON formatting. Replaying known-good premaintenance inputs against the current configuration and inspecting the raw Claude response separates malformed model output from failures introduced by downstream parsing. Clear output-format instructions and constraints are important for consistent model formatting behavior.

**Learn more:** [Prompting best practices](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/prompt-templates-and-variables) · [Handling stop reasons](https://docs.anthropic.com/pt/api/handling-stop-reasons)

definition.stemRaw:
You are a solution architect evaluating candidate use cases for a Claude-based program.  
  
For each scenario, select Yes if Claude is appropriate as the primary solution at the architectural level. Otherwise, select No.

blanks.label: drafting first-pass investigative reports from semi-structured incident logs for analyst review
computing real-time fraud scores at sub-50-millisecond latency on a streaming pipeline
long-context contract review with structured clause extraction and deviation flagging
replacing a vector index for semantic retrieval over a multi-million-document corpus
routing inbound support tickets into 30 categories with reasoning for the chosen routing

definition.explanation:
Claude is well suited to drafting reports from semi-structured text, reviewing long documents, extracting structured clauses, identifying deviations, classifying support tickets, and explaining classifications. A sub-50-ms streaming fraud decision needs predictable, low-latency specialized scoring rather than an LLM as its primary solution. Semantic retrieval across millions of documents requires a vector index or comparable retrieval system; Claude can use retrieved results but does not replace that index.

**Learn more:** [Anthropic: Prompting best practices](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/prompt-templates-and-variables) · [Anthropic: Introduction to Claude](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/welcome)

definition.stemRaw:
You are assembling factors that should guide the selection among Model Context Protocol (MCP), direct API integration, and agent-to-agent handoff.  
  
Which two factors should be included on the list? Each correct answer provides a complete solution. (Select two.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Whether the vendor publishes detailed reference documentation for each candidate protocol.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Whether the team has prior implementation experience with any of the candidate protocols.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Whether the underlying transport supports encryption in transit between the integrated services.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Whether the integration must be portable across multiple AI clients in the ecosystem.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Whether the interaction is stateless and latency-sensitive or stateful and longer-running.

definition.explanation:
Portability across multiple AI clients favors MCP because it provides a standardized client-server protocol that compatible hosts can use. Interaction lifecycle also determines the integration approach: direct APIs suit simple, low-latency request-response operations, while agent handoffs transfer control and preserve context for longer-running, stateful work between specialized agents.

**Learn more:** [MCP TypeScript SDK](https://ts.sdk.modelcontextprotocol.io/v2/) · [Running agents](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agents/running-agents)

definition.stemRaw:
You are choosing a protocol for one low-latency, stateless tool call from a Claude-based assistant to an internal pricing service that already offers a stable HTTP API.  
  
Which integration mechanism is most appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A direct API call to the existing endpoint with the appropriate scoped credentials.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A long-lived stateful session protocol for a stateless single-call interaction.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A bespoke streaming protocol layered over an unrelated asynchronous message bus.

choices.label: D
choices.text: An agent-to-agent handoff that introduces another Claude-based agent in front of the pricing service.

definition.explanation:
A direct call to the existing HTTP endpoint is the simplest and lowest-latency integration for a single stateless operation. Scoped credentials enforce least-privilege access, while a persistent session protocol, custom streaming layer, or intervening agent adds complexity and latency without serving a stated requirement. Claude supports client-side tool use, in which the application executes the tool call and returns its result.

**Learn more:** [Anthropic: Tool use overview](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/agents-and-tools/tool-use/overview)

definition.stemRaw:
You are assessing an integration specification for security weaknesses.  
  
Which two findings represent valid security gaps in the specification? Each correct answer provides a complete solution. (Select two.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Tool calls execute server-side under a least-privilege service principal scoped to the requested action.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Service credentials are placed in the prompt context, where they can leak into logs and traces.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Role-based access control is enforced only at the response-rendering layer after the model accesses restricted data.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Per-user OAuth tokens are exchanged with scope-restricted permissions and refreshed within the active session.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tool inputs and outputs are encrypted in transit using transport-layer security between services.

definition.explanation: Service credentials must not be included in prompt context because they can be exposed through logging and tracing. Authorization must be enforced before a model or tool accesses restricted data; response-layer-only RBAC allows unauthorized access to occur before rendering is blocked.

definition.stemRaw:
The platform team at Trenova Systems, Inc. must lower per-query cost and p95 latency for a high-volume Claude pipeline without reducing output quality for the core use case.  
  
Which two optimizations directly address both cost and latency at the same time? (Select two.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Enable prompt caching on the static system-prompt prefix to reduce billable input tokens on repeated calls.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Route straightforward query types to a smaller, faster Claude model and reserve the full model for complex cases.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increase max_tokens to reduce the frequency of truncated responses requiring follow-up calls.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Add a retrieval step that fetches the full source corpus into the context window before generation.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Expand the system prompt to include additional few-shot examples on every request.

definition.explanation:
Prompt caching lets repeated calls reuse a static system-prompt prefix, so cached input is billed at a lower rate and avoids reprocessing that prefix. Routing straightforward requests to a smaller, faster model lowers inference cost and response time, while reserving the larger model for complex requests preserves quality where it matters. Increasing output limits, retrieving an entire corpus, or expanding every prompt adds processing or tokens rather than directly reducing both metrics.

**Learn more:** [Anthropic Claude API pricing](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/about-claude/pricing)

definition.stemRaw:
You are implementing monitoring for a Claude-based deployment and must complete the specification steps before instrumenting the deployment.  
  
Which two steps must be completed **BEFORE** instrumenting the deployment to emit metrics and traces? Each correct answer is part of the solution. *(Select two.)*

choices.label: A
choices.text: Define the metrics and the slices the deployment will monitor across normal and adversarial traffic.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Tune the alert thresholds based on observed normal-state distributions to reduce false positives.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Define the service-level objectives (SLOs) and the error budgets the deployment will be held to.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Build the dashboards that surface metrics across slices at the cadence the team operates on.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Document the dashboards, alerts, and runbooks for the on-call rotation that will respond.

definition.explanation:
Instrumentation must be designed to emit the metrics and traffic dimensions needed to distinguish normal and adversarial behavior. Those measurements support the service-level indicators used to establish SLOs; an SLO in turn defines its error budget. Alert thresholds require observed baseline distributions, whereas dashboards and on-call documentation consume the resulting telemetry after the monitoring design is established.

**Learn more:** [Concepts in service monitoring](https://cloud.google.com/stackdriver/docs/solutions/slo-monitoring) · [OpenTelemetry Semantic Conventions](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/)

definition.stemRaw:
During discovery, you are differentiating functional requirements from non-functional requirements.  
  
Which item is a non-functional requirement?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The system must extract a defined set of specific fields from invoice attachments and populate a downstream data record.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The system must produce a draft response that a human reviewer can edit before sending.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The system must classify inbound tickets into a defined set of categories.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The system must respond at p95 latency under 800 milliseconds at the expected request volume.

definition.explanation:
A p95 latency target of under 800 milliseconds at the expected request volume is a measurable performance constraint that specifies how well the system must operate. Field extraction, human-editable draft generation, and ticket classification specify functions the system must perform. Microsoft defines functional requirements as what an application does and non-functional requirements as how well it performs, including latency.

**Learn more:** [Build for business needs - Azure Architecture Center](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/architecture/guide/design-principles/build-for-business)

definition.stemRaw:
A healthcare organization is assessing two Claude-powered AI architectures for a clinical-documentation assistant. Architecture X delivers higher output-quality scores, but costs $0.18 per documentation session and averages 4.2 seconds per response. Architecture Y scores slightly lower on quality metrics, but costs $0.09 per session and averages 2.1 seconds per response. The stated SLA requires responses in under 3 seconds, and the projected annual volume is 2 million documentation sessions.  
  
Which evaluation approach properly applies business-value pillar analysis to this decision?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Select Architecture Y based solely on the 50% cost reduction, since solution cost is the most important value pillar in healthcare budget-constrained environments.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Select Architecture X because the higher quality scores justify the cost premium, and any SLA gap can be addressed through infrastructure optimization after deployment.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Eliminate Architecture X on SLA grounds, then evaluate Architecture Y against the efficiency and solution cost pillars by calculating annual cost difference and assessing whether the quality delta materially impacts clinical workflow productivity.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Recommend a hybrid approach using Architecture X for complex cases and Architecture Y for routine cases, without additional analysis, since this preserves quality where it matters most.

definition.stemRaw:
You are troubleshooting a Claude Code session in which its subagent uses 50,000 context tokens before the engineer types even a single message.  
  
Which root cause is most likely?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The developer's keyboard layout or input-method configuration is the cause of the elevated context consumption, introducing extra tokens before the engineer types any message.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Many MCP servers are configured, each contributing tool definitions to the context budget; Tool Search is not enabled, so all definitions load upfront.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The model has internal personal preferences or default behaviors that silently consume large portions of context budget before any user message is processed, independent of tool configuration.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The font rendering or display-scaling settings of the IDE are converting visual output into additional context tokens, causing the high pre-session context consumption.

definition.explanation:
When Tool Search is disabled, Claude Code loads all configured MCP tool definitions into the context window at startup. A large collection of MCP servers can therefore consume tens of thousands of tokens before any engineer message is entered.

**Learn more:** [Connect Claude Code to tools via MCP](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp) · [Tool search tool](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/tool-search-tool)

definition.stemRaw:
You are assisting an engineer whose newly added MCP server is not appearing in their Claude Code session.  
  
Which diagnostic step should be attempted first?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Disable every MCP server in the configuration to isolate the issue, removing all tool access rather than confirming whether the new server is registered.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Switch the team to a different Claude product family unrelated to the existing workflow, abandoning the current configuration rather than diagnosing the registration issue.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Verify the MCP server is registered using the listing command, then reconnect the session if needed, since configuration changes typically require a restart to take effect.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reinstall the developer’s operating system from scratch, discarding all local configuration and tool state before attempting any targeted diagnostic steps.

definition.explanation:
`claude mcp list` confirms whether an MCP server is configured and reports its health status, such as connected, authentication required, or failed to connect. This establishes whether the issue is registration or session connectivity before taking disruptive action; reconnecting the session can refresh the active MCP state when necessary.

**Learn more:** [Connect Claude Code to tools via MCP](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp)

definition.stemRaw:
You are identifying characteristics of strong architectural-decision communication.  
  
Which two characteristics should be included on the list? Each correct answer represents a complete solution. (Select two.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ownership and review cadence for revisiting the decision when conditions or assumptions change.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Distribution to a standing review forum with mandatory attendance from senior engineering leaders.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Omission of rejected alternatives to keep the decision document focused and concise for readers.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Alternatives considered along with the criteria that were used to evaluate each alternative.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Use of a consistent template across the team to standardize the visual presentation of decisions.

definition.explanation:
Strong architectural decision records communicate both accountability and rationale. Ownership with a review cadence keeps a decision maintainable as its assumptions or conditions change, while documenting considered alternatives and their evaluation criteria makes the trade-offs and justification understandable to current and future stakeholders. Official ADR guidance calls for ownership and for recording the context, including possible solutions considered and the decision’s consequences.

**Learn more:** [Architectural decision record process - AWS Prescriptive Guidance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/architectural-decision-records/adr-process.html) · [FAQ about architectural decision records - AWS Prescriptive Guidance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/architectural-decision-records/faq.html)

definition.stemRaw:
A Claude architect is designing a HIPAA-compliant pipeline that handles patient records.  
  
Which two design decisions directly support HIPAA compliance requirements? (Select two.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Setting max_tokens to a low value to minimize the volume of text generated per request.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Selecting the highest-capability Claude model to maximize diagnostic accuracy.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Enforcing role-based access controls so that PHI is retrievable only by authorized personnel.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ensuring patient data is never included in training feedback loops sent to the model provider without a BAA in place.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Using streaming responses to reduce perceived latency for clinical users.

definition.explanation:
HIPAA safeguards include access controls that restrict electronic protected health information (ePHI) to authorized workforce members. When a service provider receives PHI as part of performing services, a business associate agreement (BAA) must define and restrict permitted uses and disclosures and require appropriate safeguards; PHI therefore must not be sent to a model provider for training feedback without an applicable BAA.

**Learn more:** [Business Associates](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/privacy/guidance/business-associates/index.html) · [Collecting, Using, or Sharing Consumer Health Information?](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/special-topics/hipaa-ftc-act/index.html)

definition.stemRaw:
An architect reviews a set of architecture-documentation packages before transferring a Claude-based pipeline to an implementation team.  
  
Which two characteristics show that a documentation package is sufficient to enable implementation without continued involvement from the architect? (Select two.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: The document specifies integration contracts, configuration schemas, and expected input/output shapes for each component.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The document includes a decision log that records the rationale for key architectural choices and the alternatives rejected.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The document provides a high-level narrative description of the business problem without component-level detail.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The document includes the architect’s contact information for questions arising during implementation.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The document lists all Claude models that were evaluated but does not specify which was selected or why.

definition.explanation: Implementation teams need explicit integration contracts, configuration schemas, and expected input/output shapes to build and connect components correctly. A decision log also preserves the rationale for key architectural choices and rejected alternatives, allowing the team to apply the intended trade-offs without relying on the architect.

definition.stemRaw:
The engineering lead at Trenova Systems, Inc. is assessing two proposals to improve developer workflows with Claude-assisted tooling. Proposal A integrates Claude Code into the IDE for inline code generation and review. Proposal B sends all code-generation requests through a shared Slack bot with no IDE integration.  
  
Which two observations most accurately assess these proposals against workflow-improvement objectives? (Select two.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Proposal B is superior because centralizing requests in Slack creates an auditable log of all code-generation activity.

choices.label: B

A Claude architect is setting up a shared Claude Code environment for a 12-person development team.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Commit shared MCP server definitions and tool permissions in project-scope configuration files alongside the repository.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Apply managed configuration to enforce non-overridable security and compliance policies across all team members.

choices.label: C

choices.label: D

Project-scoped configuration can be committed with the repository so all contributors receive the same MCP server definitions and tool-permission baseline. Managed configuration takes precedence over user and project settings and cannot be overridden, enabling organization-wide enforcement of security and compliance policies. An outbound tool allow-list, destination restrictions, and per-call approval constrain where an agent can transmit information, mitigating data exfiltration through tool calls. definition.stemRaw:
A Claude Architect reviews a post-deployment performance report for an AI-assisted legal-document summarization system.  
  
The report contains these observations:  
  
1. Average summarization time decreased from 47 minutes to 6 minutes per document.  
2. Associates spend less time on summaries, but overall billable output has not measurably changed.  
3. Infrastructure costs increased by 22% because redundant retry logic generated additional API calls.  
4. Some summaries require attorney correction, adding an average of 8 minutes of review per document.  
  
Which analysis correctly assigns each observation to the appropriate business-value pillar?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Observations 1 and 2 both indicate efficiency gains; Observation 3 is a solution-cost issue; Observation 4 is a performance-SLA issue.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Observation 1 is a transformation outcome; Observation 2 is an efficiency gain; Observation 3 is a performance-SLA degradation; Observation 4 is a solution-cost issue.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Observations 1 and 4 together indicate a net performance-SLA improvement; Observation 2 is a transformation gap; Observation 3 is a productivity drain from over-engineering.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Observation 1 indicates an efficiency gain; Observation 2 shows that productivity has not yet been realized; Observation 3 is a solution-cost issue; Observation 4 is an efficiency loss that partially offsets Observation 1.

definition.explanation: Reducing summarization time is an efficiency gain because it lowers labor time per document. Reduced effort does not become a productivity gain until it produces measurable additional billable output or other realized output. Extra API calls that raise infrastructure spending are a solution-cost issue. Attorney correction time adds work back into the process, creating an efficiency loss that partially offsets the time saved by automated summarization.

A research-summarization assistant has been in production for six months. A user reports that a generated summary included a fabricated citation. The product team asks whether the incident needs architectural action or is an isolated occurrence.  
  
Which two Diligence-competency actions should you take? Each correct answer represents part of the solution. *(Select two.)*

choices.label: A
choices.text: Sample recent summaries to estimate the fabrication frequency across the population.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Disable the assistant immediately for all current users without any prior diagnostic analysis.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Review whether citation-grounding controls exist anywhere in the current generation pipeline.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Communicate to users that the assistant does not fabricate output as a matter of design.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Treat the incident as an anecdotal isolated case and take no further investigative action.

definition.explanation:
Assessing a sample of recent summaries establishes whether citation fabrication is a broader production-quality problem and provides evidence for deciding its scope. Reviewing the generation pipeline for citation-grounding controls identifies whether the system has effective mechanisms to tie citations to supporting sources and expose a systemic architectural gap. NIST describes systematic evaluation of factual grounding and automated citation evaluation, while Microsoft recommends validation and monitoring of retrieval and grounding components.

**Learn more:** [Building Evaluation Probes into Agentic AI](https://www.nist.gov/programs-projects/building-evaluation-probes-agentic-ai) · [Grounding Data Compromise (Retrieval Layer)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/security/zero-trust/catalog-ai-attack-techniques/grounding-data-compromise)

definition.stemRaw:
You are presenting an architecture decision to a mixed audience that includes an executive sponsor and the engineering leads responsible for implementing the decision.  
  
Which presentation approach best serves both audiences?

choices.label: A

choices.label: C

choices.label: D

definition.explanation: An effective architecture-decision presentation starts with the decision, the business outcomes it supports, and the trade-offs accepted so executive stakeholders can assess value and risk. It then supplies the technical rationale, alternatives considered, and implementation implications needed by engineering leads to validate and carry out the decision.

definition.stemRaw:
You are identifying characteristics of robust guardrail design for an enterprise deployment.  
  
Which two characteristics should be on the list? Each correct answer provides a complete solution. (Select two.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Centralized log retention for guardrail violations with quarterly review by the security team.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Per-role tool allow-lists enforced at the orchestration layer before any tool call executes.

choices.label: C
choices.text: User feedback channels that route reported guardrail failures into the product backlog for triage.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Periodic refresh of the system prompt wording to keep refusal language current and clear.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Adversarial-input coverage in the evaluation set with regression tracking on guardrail performance.

definition.explanation:
Robust enterprise guardrails enforce least privilege at the action boundary: a role-specific tool allow-list prevents an unauthorized tool call before it executes, rather than relying on a model instruction to decline it. Guardrail quality also needs repeatable adversarial testing and regression tracking so prompt-injection and other bypass attempts are covered and deteriorations are detected over time. OpenAI’s guidance supports limiting allowed tools and red-teaming applications against adversarial input.

**Learn more:** [MCP connections | OpenAI API](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agents-api/tools/mcp) · [Safety best practices | OpenAI API](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/safety-best-practices)

Explicitly reconciling differing stakeholder positions resolves substantive conflicts instead of leaving them hidden, creating durable alignment.

definition.stemRaw:
You are establishing an SLA for a Claude-based assistant.  
  
Which SLA definition is the most operationally meaningful?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A target tied to a stakeholder sentiment measure such as “the team feels satisfied,” which cannot be measured objectively or used to trigger a documented breach response.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A measurable target with a defined metric, threshold, evaluation window, and consequence for breach—for example, “p95 per-request latency under 800 ms over a 28-day window.”

choices.label: C

choices.label: D

definition.explanation: An operational SLA defines an objective metric, an acceptable threshold, the time window used to evaluate compliance, and a documented consequence or response for a breach. These elements make performance measurable and establish when remediation is required.
