You are establishing transparency practices for a customer-facing assistant whose responses are materially influenced by AI.  
  
Which transparency practice most directly promotes responsible deployment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Misrepresent the AI’s role in producing responses in order to make the assistant feel more trustworthy or more human, undermining informed user consent and organizational transparency.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Refuse to answer any user question about how the responses were produced or whether AI was involved, treating the AI’s role as confidential operational information.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Disclose AI involvement to end users in line with the organization’s transparency policy and provide a documented path to reach a human when needed.

choices.label: D

definition.explanation:
Responsible deployment requires clear disclosure of AI involvement to the people affected by the system, enabling them to understand the nature of the interaction and calibrate their reliance appropriately. A documented, accessible path to human assistance also supports oversight and escalation when the assistant cannot appropriately resolve a need. Microsoft guidance calls for clear AI disclosure for external-facing agents and visible human handoff or interaction options.

You are auditing a procurement-assistant agent whose defined responsibility is drafting purchase requests for review. For each currently configured tool, select Yes if it should remain after a least-privilege audit. Otherwise, select No if it should be removed.  
  
For each of the following statements, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

an inbox-send tool that emails purchase requests to vendors directly
a draft-write tool that creates purchase-request drafts in the review queue
a production-database admin tool unrelated to procurement
A read-only policy-document tool that returns the relevant procurement policies

definition.explanation: Least privilege permits the read-only catalog and policy lookups needed to prepare compliant purchase-request drafts, plus the draft-write capability required to place drafts in the review queue. Direct vendor email sending exceeds the review-only responsibility, and unrelated production-database administration is unnecessary and overly privileged.

definition.stemRaw:
You are establishing escalation criteria for ambiguous cases in an automated workflow.  
  
Which set of criteria best enables consistent escalation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: No escalation criteria; the model decides independently on every turn whether to escalate, without explicit confidence thresholds, impact categories, or classifier-based ambiguity flags.

choices.label: B

choices.label: C
choices.text: Escalation at the discretion of whoever is available when the team’s on-call engineer has spare capacity, without a defined threshold, category, or ambiguity criterion.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A confidence score below a defined threshold, presence of high-impact decision categories, ambiguity flags raised by content classifiers, and the user’s explicit request for review.

definition.explanation: Consistent escalation depends on explicit, repeatable triggers: a defined confidence threshold, designated high-impact decision categories, classifier-based ambiguity signals, and a user request for review. These criteria enable the workflow to identify cases requiring human oversight before a potentially consequential automated decision is finalized.

definition.stemRaw:
A loan pre-qualification assistant produces approval recommendations that agree with the human underwriter’s decision 94 percent of the time. The fairness team has evaluated approval-rate parity across protected groups and found no significant difference. A board member asks whether this evidence is enough to declare the assistant fair.  
  
Which two Discernment-competency findings should you report? Each correct answer provides part of the solution. (Select two.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Approval rate parity does not by itself assess error rate parity across protected groups.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Match with human underwriters does not establish freedom from underwriter-introduced bias.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The 94 percent match rate is sufficient evidence of fairness for the assistant’s decisions.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The fairness team’s review process likely missed at least some of the protected groups studied.

choices.label: E
choices.text: A larger sample is needed before any meaningful fairness claim can be made about the model.

definition.explanation: Approval-rate parity alone does not determine whether error rates, such as false-positive or false-negative rates, are comparable across protected groups. Agreement with human underwriters also does not prove fairness, because the assistant can learn and perpetuate bias embedded in the human decisions used as its reference.

definition.stemRaw:

Which integration design best meets this requirement?

A product manager has asked whether extra guardrails are required in the application layer, or whether the Skill alone is adequate.  
  
Which two guardrail responsibilities must remain at the application layer instead of the Skill? Each correct answer represents part of the solution. (Select two.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Log every generated summary to the firm’s compliance audit trail for retention.

choices.label: B

choices.label: C

choices.label: D

choices.label: E

Authorization is an application-level access-control decision because it depends on the requesting user’s identity and permissions. Compliance-audit retention is also an application-level responsibility because the application must reliably record every generated summary in the firm’s audit trail. The approved Skill can centrally apply the reusable disclaimer and prohibited-language content controls. Anthropic’s guidance describes centralized authentication and audit logging as infrastructure or gateway capabilities surrounding model interactions.

**Learn more:** [LLM gateway configuration - Anthropic](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code/llm-gateway)

definition.stemRaw:

definition.stemRaw:
You are deploying a standardized Claude Code configuration to an engineering team and need to complete the planning activities before piloting the configuration.  
  
Which two steps must be completed **BEFORE** piloting the configuration with a small group of engineers? Each correct answer represents part of the solution. *(Select two.)*

choices.label: A
choices.text: Define the project-scope baseline covering Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, permission rules, and subagents.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Onboard every engineer in the organization to the new configuration through mandatory training sessions.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Roll out the stabilized configuration to additional teams with documentation and a defined support channel.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Identify the team workflows, security boundaries, and which decisions belong to managed configuration versus project scope.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Iterate the configuration based on the pilot findings and stabilize the baseline before broader rollout.

definition.explanation:
A controlled pilot requires defining the applicable team workflows and security boundaries, including which controls must be centrally managed and which belong to a project. That decision enables a project-scope baseline for shared MCP servers, permission rules, and subagents. Claude Code distinguishes centrally managed settings from shared project settings, and project-scoped MCP servers are intended for team-shared configuration. Organization-wide training, broader rollout, and post-pilot refinement follow rather than precede the pilot.

**Learn more:** [Claude Code on Console to Enterprise migration](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/14128775-claude-code-on-console-to-enterprise-migration) · [Connect Claude Code to tools through MCP](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code/mcp)

definition.stemRaw:
You are assembling a diagnostic toolkit for Claude Code operational problems.  
  
Which two diagnostic actions should be included in the toolkit? Each correct answer provides a complete solution. (Select two.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Increase the model sampling temperature so that intermittent issues surface more frequently for analysis.

choices.label: B
choices.text: File a support ticket with vendor support before any local reproduction or evidence collection.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Reproduce the issue with a minimal reproduction case that isolates one variable at a time.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Roll back to the previous Claude Code version immediately to confirm whether the issue is version specific.

choices.label: E
choices.text: List the configured Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers and inspect server status to identify connection failures.

definition.explanation:
A minimal reproduction that isolates one variable at a time establishes whether a specific input, configuration, or environment condition causes the failure and yields actionable evidence. MCP servers are external operational dependencies; Claude Code documents MCP server management and status, so listing configured servers and inspecting their status can expose connection or configuration failures. Support escalation is more effective after diagnostic evidence has been gathered, while changing model temperature or immediately rolling back a version does not constitute a complete, targeted diagnostic method.

**Learn more:** [Connect Claude Code to tools via MCP](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp) · [Troubleshoot Claude Code installation and authentication](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/14552646-troubleshoot-claude-code-installation-and-authentication)

definition.stemRaw:
You are incorporating Claude Code into a workflow that operates against a production database.  
  
Which guardrail design most directly maintains safety for data-modifying operations?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Allow Claude Code to write directly to the production database without subagent scoping, read-only credential defaults, or human confirmation gates on data-modifying operations.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Configure the database MCP server with a fully privileged credential that can perform any read or write operation, and allow all operations to proceed without explicit human confirmation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Disable all logging and auditing on database operations through the MCP server to reduce alert noise, removing the observability needed to detect unintended data modifications.

choices.label: D

definition.explanation:
A read-only database credential and a tool list limited to read-only operations prevent unintended writes by default, while explicit human confirmation provides an approval gate before any data-changing action. This applies defense in depth and least privilege to production access. Claude Code supports restricting available tools and permission prompts for actions that require approval.

**Learn more:** [Claude Code CLI reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-usage) · [Claude Code Security](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/security)

choices.label: B
