definition.explanation: A complete implementation handoff needs an architecture overview and ADRs to convey the system design and rationale; component contracts to define integration boundaries; an evaluation framework with a reference set to validate behavior; runbooks and an on-call playbook to support operations; and a known-limitations record to make risks and constraints explicit.

definition.stemRaw:
You are identifying indicators that a deployment should return to design instead of continuing to iterate in place.  
  
Which indicator most directly shows that a new design cycle is needed?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A runbook step requires a clarification edit to improve on-call guidance accuracy, which can be handled as a documentation update without changes to component responsibilities or core contracts.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A dashboard alert threshold needs a small numerical adjustment to reduce false-positive noise, which can be handled as an operational configuration change without a new design cycle.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A minor copy edit is requested in a customer-facing string within the existing UI, which can be handled as a localized content change without altering component responsibilities or contracts.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The system’s current architecture cannot meet the new requirements without changes to component responsibilities or core contracts.

definition.explanation: A new design cycle is needed when new requirements cannot be met within the current architecture without changing component responsibilities or core contracts. Those changes alter fundamental design boundaries rather than making a localized operational, documentation, configuration, or content update.

definition.stemRaw:
A Claude architect notices that, after a recent model-version upgrade, grounded responses started to include claims that are not supported by the retrieved source documents.  
  
Which mitigation most directly addresses this failure mode?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Constrain responses to source-supported content, require citations, and add a verification step.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Score each new model version against a stable adversarial evaluation set.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Replace the shared API key with per-user OAuth tokens to restrict data access.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Treat retrieved data as untrusted and apply input classifiers at ingestion time.

definition.explanation: Source-grounding constraints, mandatory citations, and a verification step directly reduce unsupported claims by requiring response content to be traceable to and checked against the retrieved documents.

definition.stemRaw:
You are reviewing a colleague’s Claude Code permission rules for an enterprise rollout. The rules provide unrestricted Bash access across all projects for every developer.  
  
Which response is most appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Add unrestricted access to additional tool categories as well, so that Bash is not asymmetrically more permissive than other tools, expanding the attack surface further in the name of consistency.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Approve the unrestricted Bash access as written on the grounds that narrowing the rules would add configuration complexity, accepting the full attack surface for all engineers across all projects.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Replace unrestricted Bash with narrowly scoped tool patterns that allow only the specific commands the workflows require, and add explicit deny rules for sensitive operations.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Disable all permission rules for the enterprise rollout so every command across every project runs without any tool-pattern scoping or explicit deny rules for sensitive operations.

definition.explanation:
Enterprise Claude Code permissions should follow least privilege: allow only the Bash command patterns required by approved workflows and explicitly deny sensitive operations. Claude Code supports scoped `Bash(...)` allow patterns and a `--disallowedTools` mechanism, avoiding the security risk of arbitrary shell execution across all projects.

**Learn more:** [Claude Code CLI reference](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code/cli-usage)

definition.stemRaw:
A solutions architect is reviewing stakeholder feedback gathered after the first quarter of a Claude-powered procurement automation deployment.  
  
The feedback contains four statements:  
  
(1) “Our procurement team is processing 3x more purchase orders per analyst per day.”  
  
(2) “We have eliminated the manual data entry role entirely and redeployed those staff to vendor relationship management.”  
  
(3) “The API integration costs are running 40% over the projected per-transaction budget.”  
  
(4) “Response latency during end-of-month batch runs is averaging 11 seconds, against our committed 5-second SLA.”  
  
Which option correctly identifies the primary business-value pillar represented by each stakeholder statement?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Statement 1: Efficiency; Statement 2: Transformation; Statement 3: Solution Cost; Statement 4: Performance SLA

choices.label: B
choices.text: Statement 1: Productivity; Statement 2: Efficiency; Statement 3: Solution Cost; Statement 4: Performance SLA

choices.label: C
choices.text: Statement 1: Transformation; Statement 2: Productivity; Statement 3: Solution Cost; Statement 4: Efficiency

choices.label: D
choices.text: Statement 1: Efficiency; Statement 2: Productivity; Statement 3: Performance SLA; Statement 4: Solution Cost

definition.explanation:
Processing three times as many purchase orders per analyst increases throughput and reduces effort per transaction within the existing workflow, which is Efficiency. Eliminating manual data-entry work and moving staff to vendor relationship management redesigns responsibilities around higher-value work, which is Transformation. A 40% API-cost overrun is a Solution Cost concern, while 11-second latency against a committed 5-second target is a Performance SLA issue. Anthropic describes automation that frees professionals for strategic work as transforming the workflow.

**Learn more:** [Campfire accelerates accounting with Claude](https://www.anthropic.com/customers/campfire) · [Create business value with Claude](https://assets.anthropic.com/m/66daaa23018ab0fd/original/Anthropic-enterprise-ebook-digital.pdf)

definition.stemRaw:
You are creating an architecture guide for a new deployment and must finish the planning activities before drafting each guide section.  
  
Which two activities must be completed **BEFORE** drafting every section of the guide? Each correct answer represents part of the solution. *(Select two.)*

choices.label: A
choices.text: Identify the audience and the questions the guide must answer for that audience.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Translate the guide into the supported regional languages for the candidate population.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Validate the guide with the implementation team and incorporate corrections.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Establish the document under version control with a defined review cadence and approver list.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Outline the guide sections covering the overview, components, contracts, flows, runbooks, and limitations.

definition.explanation: An architecture guide must be planned around its target audience and the information that audience needs. It must also have an outline that organizes the required content—such as the overview, components, contracts, flows, runbooks, and limitations—before individual sections are drafted.

definition.stemRaw:
You are supporting an EU-based deployment subject to GDPR obligations.  
  
Which combination of measures best supports the deployment’s GDPR posture?

choices.label: A
choices.text: enterprise-tier deployment with a signed Data Processing Addendum, defined data-retention configuration, redaction of personal data not needed for the task, and documented data-subject-rights handling

choices.label: B
choices.text: disabling all data-retention configuration, redaction controls, and data-subject-rights handling to simplify day-to-day operations, accepting the resulting GDPR compliance exposure

choices.label: C
choices.text: using a personal Claude account tier for processing EU personal data at scale, with no signed Data Processing Addendum and no documented data-subject-rights handling procedure

choices.label: D
choices.text: pasting full EU personal data into every prompt to “give Claude complete context” without considering purpose limitation, data minimization, or the organization’s Data Processing Addendum obligations

definition.explanation:
GDPR requires personal data to be limited to what is necessary, retained no longer than necessary, and processed by a service provider under an appropriate binding processor arrangement. Redacting unnecessary personal data, defining retention, maintaining a Data Processing Addendum, and documenting procedures for data-subject rights support these obligations. Claude Enterprise also provides configurable data-retention controls.

**Learn more:** [Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX%3A32016R0679) · [Custom Data Retention Controls for Claude Enterprise](https://privacy.anthropic.com/en/articles/10440198-custom-data-retention-controls-for-claude-enterprise)

definition.stemRaw:
You support a team whose Claude Code sessions routinely load 60 or more MCP tools from numerous servers, exhausting the context budget before a session starts.  
  
Which change most directly resolves this problem without removing capability?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Enable Tool Search so tool definitions are deferred and discovered on demand rather than loaded into context upfront.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Disable every MCP server in the configuration to free up context budget, accepting that the team loses all tool access and cannot perform any MCP-dependent task in the session.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increase the prompt’s verbosity with additional instructions and context, which consumes more of the context budget rather than reducing the tool-definition overhead causing the issue.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Add additional MCP servers to give the team more capability, which increases rather than reduces the number of tool definitions loaded into the session’s context budget.

definition.explanation:
Tool Search supports deferred loading, which prevents deferred MCP tool descriptions from entering the model’s initial context. The tools remain available and their definitions load on demand when discovered through search, reducing initial context overhead without removing MCP capability.

**Learn more:** [Tool search tool — Claude Platform Docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/tool-search-tool) · [MCP connector — Claude Platform Docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-connector)

definition.stemRaw:
During an architecture review, the security team identifies a risk that adversarial content inserted into retrieved documents could influence the model’s behavior.  
  
Which mitigation most directly addresses this threat?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Treat all retrieved content as untrusted input and apply input classifiers with output validation.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Require citations for each claim and constrain responses to source-supported content.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Restrict outbound tool calls to an approved destination allow-list.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Score outputs against a stable adversarial evaluation set on each model-version change.

definition.explanation:
Retrieved documents can carry indirect prompt-injection instructions. Treating all retrieved content as untrusted, applying classifiers or injection detection before it reaches the model, and validating outputs establishes controls at the relevant trust boundary.

**Learn more:** [Retrieval augmented generation (RAG) and indexes in Microsoft Foundry](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/concepts/retrieval-augmented-generation) · [Prompt Injection (Direct / Indirect)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/security/zero-trust/catalog-ai-attack-techniques/prompt-injection)

definition.stemRaw:
You are selecting the appropriate level of detail for an implementation guide. The audience is a delivery team that will build the deployment.  
  
Which guidance composition best supports them?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Component responsibilities, contracts between components, sequence diagrams of the dominant flows, configuration parameters with defaults, and operational runbooks.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Component responsibilities and interface contracts only, without sequence diagrams of the dominant flows, configuration parameters with defaults, or runbooks to guide operational tasks.

choices.label: C
choices.text: An architecture overview and sequence diagrams for the dominant flows, without interface contracts, configuration-parameter tables, or operational runbooks for the delivery team to follow.

choices.label: D
choices.text: An architecture overview and a list of known limitations, without component-level diagrams, interface contracts, configuration parameters, or operational runbooks to support implementation.

definition.explanation: A delivery team needs implementation-level guidance covering component responsibilities, contracts between components, dominant-flow sequences, configuration parameters and defaults, and operational procedures. Together, these artifacts support building, integrating, configuring, and operating the deployment.

definition.stemRaw:
You are incorporating Claude Code into a team workflow and must complete the design and configuration steps before piloting the integrated workflow with a small group.  
  
Which two steps must be completed BEFORE piloting the integrated workflow? Each correct answer represents part of the solution. (Select two.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Document the integrated workflow with handoff criteria, permission boundaries, and on-call runbooks.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Identify the workflow steps where AI-assisted tooling adds value and where human authority must remain.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Negotiate the workflow change with affected teams and obtain formal sign-off from each manager.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Iterate the integrated workflow based on pilot findings before broader rollout to the team.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Configure the project-scope MCP servers, permissions, subagents, and persistent project context.

definition.explanation:
A Claude Code pilot needs an explicit division between workflow activities where AI assistance adds value and activities that remain under human authority. It also needs the project’s operational configuration in place: MCP integrations, permission controls, specialized subagents, and persistent project instructions/context. Claude Code documents project-scoped MCP setup, permissions, subagents, and project memory as distinct configuration mechanisms that establish those capabilities and boundaries.

**Learn more:** [Claude Code Commands](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/commands) · [Connect Claude Code to tools via MCP](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp)

definition.stemRaw:
You are documenting an architectural decision to enable future audit and onboarding.  
  
Which artifact is the best fit?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A slide deck in a presentation folder with no accompanying written rationale.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A code comment in a single file that contains an opinion of one engineer.

choices.label: C
choices.text: An Architecture Decision Record that states the context, the decision, the alternatives considered, the consequences, and the date and authors.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A short verbal note shared during a hallway conversation with no written record.

definition.explanation:
An Architecture Decision Record preserves the context and rationale for an architectural choice, including alternatives, decision outcome, and consequences. Its written, attributable record supports later audits and helps new team members understand why the architecture took its current form.

**Learn more:** [Maintain an architecture decision record (ADR)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/well-architected/architect-role/architecture-decision-record)

definition.stemRaw:
You are a platform architect building an internal Claude-based assistant for both finance analysts and external auditors. Each group must be able to access only the documents authorized for its role.  
  
At which point in the pipeline should role-based access control be enforced?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Inside the system prompt as a natural-language instruction for Claude to ignore unauthorized documents.

choices.label: B
choices.text: At the retrieval layer, before any role-restricted content reaches the prompt-construction step or the model.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Nowhere in the pipeline; rely on the model’s general refusal behavior to reject unauthorized document access without any enforced access control.

choices.label: D
choices.text: After the response is generated, by post-filtering content that should not have been retrieved.

definition.explanation:
Role-based access control belongs at retrieval time, before retrieved documents are added to the prompt or exposed to the model. Enforcing authorization there prevents unauthorized content from entering the model context; prompt-only instructions, general refusal behavior, and post-response filtering do not provide that security boundary. Amazon Bedrock documents ACL-aware retrieval as pre-retrieval filtering that returns only documents the supplied user is permitted to access.

**Learn more:** [Access Control Lists awareness enablement - Amazon Bedrock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/kb-managed-acl.html) · [Retrieve - Amazon Bedrock API Reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/APIReference/API_agent-runtime_Retrieve.html)

definition.stemRaw:
A Claude architect is implementing safety controls for a customer-facing advice assistant that must never give regulated investment recommendations.  
  
Which two guardrail implementations most directly enforce this requirement? (Select two.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Increase response temperature to introduce variability that reduces the likelihood of specific recommendations.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Add an output classifier that detects and blocks responses containing regulated investment-recommendation language.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Limit session length to reduce the volume of queries processed per user per day.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Log all user queries to a SIEM for post-hoc compliance review.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Define explicit out-of-scope categories in the system prompt with fixed refusal phrasing for investment advice requests.

definition.explanation:
An output classifier can block prohibited investment-recommendation language before it is delivered, while explicit system-prompt boundaries and prescribed refusal wording direct the assistant to decline out-of-scope investment-advice requests. Anthropic guidance recommends strengthened system prompts that state legal and ethical boundaries and how to refuse, and describes filters as a way to enforce output guardrails.

**Learn more:** [Anthropic: Mitigating jailbreaks and prompt injection](https://platform.claude.com/docs/ko/test-and-evaluate/strengthen-guardrails/mitigate-jailbreaks) · [Anthropic: Customer support agent guide](https://platform.claude.com/docs/de/about-claude/use-case-guides/customer-support-chat)

definition.stemRaw:
A business sponsor has asked for an AI solution to “improve customer experience.” The sponsor cannot specify which customer journey is failing, which metric demonstrates that failure, or which decisions the AI should support. The sponsor is asking you to start design work next week.  
  
Which delegation-competency action should you take first?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Recommend that the sponsor revise the request and resubmit it later for evaluation.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Begin prototyping a generic assistant against the broad request before the next deadline.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Propose a fixed scope that you commit to by default based on your own assumptions.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Facilitate a structured discovery to define the failing decision and the target metric.

definition.explanation: A structured discovery session establishes the specific failing decision, the affected customer journey, and a measurable target outcome before solution design begins. These definitions provide the problem scope and success criteria needed to determine whether AI is appropriate and what it should support.

definition.stemRaw:
You are evaluating data-exfiltration risk in a Claude-based assistant that has tools for internal-document retrieval and outbound HTTP calls.  
  
Which scenario most directly signals a data-exfiltration risk?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The outbound HTTP tool returns a 200 response when the assistant calls an allow-listed domain to fulfil a user-initiated data-lookup request.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The user submits a routine question and receives a routine answer.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Adversarial content in a retrieved document instructs the model to call the outbound HTTP tool and send sensitive content to an attacker-controlled URL.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The internal-document retrieval tool returns a document that the user is authorized to view.

definition.explanation:
Adversarial instructions embedded in retrieved content can redirect an assistant to invoke an outbound tool and transmit sensitive data to an attacker-controlled endpoint. This is an indirect prompt-injection path that enables unauthorized data exfiltration.

**Learn more:** [Mitigate jailbreaks and prompt injections — Claude Platform Docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/test-and-evaluate/strengthen-guardrails/mitigate-jailbreaks)

definition.stemRaw:
A Claude architect must ensure that, once it is set, a security-hardening flag cannot be disabled by any individual engineer.  
  
Which configuration scope correctly enforces this requirement?

choices.label: A
choices.text: User scope (~/.claude/settings.json) on each engineer’s machine

choices.label: B
choices.text: Environment variable defined in the CI/CD pipeline only

choices.label: C
choices.text: Managed configuration applied centrally and marked as non-overridable

choices.label: D
choices.text: Project scope (.claude/settings.json) committed to the repository

definition.explanation:
Claude Code applies centrally deployed managed settings above user, project, local, and command-line configuration, preventing an engineer from overriding an enforced security policy. A managed policy is therefore the appropriate scope for an organization-wide non-overridable hardening flag.

**Learn more:** [Deploy managed settings - Claude Code Docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/managed-settings)

definition.stemRaw:
You are setting up a HIPAA-eligible deployment for a healthcare customer.  
  
Which configuration enables HIPAA compliance when using Anthropic-provided tools?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Claude Free with no contractual addendum, since consumer products meet HIPAA requirements out of the box.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Claude Enterprise with a signed Business Associate Agreement, Zero Data Retention enabled, and audit logging configured for compliance tracking.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Disabling all audit logging so that no PHI is recorded in any log store, on the assumption that the absence of logs satisfies HIPAA requirements without a signed BAA.

choices.label: D
choices.text: An ad-hoc personal Claude account used by individual clinicians for PHI-related tasks, with no Business Associate Agreement, no Zero Data Retention, and no audit logging configured.

definition.explanation:
A HIPAA-eligible Anthropic deployment must be covered by an appropriate Business Associate Agreement for an approved service. Zero Data Retention and audit logging support the required handling and accountability controls, whereas consumer and personal accounts without a BAA do not provide that contractual HIPAA coverage. The deployment must also follow Anthropic’s HIPAA-specific configuration and feature limitations.

**Learn more:** [Business Associate Agreements (BAA) for Commercial Customers](https://privacy.anthropic.com/en/articles/8114513-business-associate-agreements-baa-for-commercial-customers) · [Anthropic Trust Center](https://trust.anthropic.com/)

definition.stemRaw:
A Claude architect is leading the discovery phase of a new AI-powered customer-service solution.  
  
Which two activities are typical of structured discovery and requirements gathering for a Claude-based deployment? (Select two.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Facilitating stakeholder workshops to surface latency, accuracy, and compliance constraints before scoping begins.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Selecting the Claude model tier based on the architect’s prior project experience before stakeholder input is collected.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Generating an initial prototype and iterating based on user reaction rather than written requirements.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Documenting explicit success criteria and failure thresholds that will gate production deployment.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Deferring constraint documentation until the integration design phase to avoid scope creep.

definition.explanation:
Structured discovery elicits operational, performance, and compliance constraints from stakeholders before scoping so the solution can be designed against real requirements. Production readiness also depends on explicit, measurable success criteria and failure thresholds that can serve as deployment gates. Anthropic guidance recommends defining measurable success criteria and evaluating customer-support implementations against established benchmarks.

**Learn more:** [Define success criteria — Claude Platform Docs](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/test-and-evaluate/define-success) · [Customer support agent — Claude Platform Docs](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/about-claude/use-case-guides/customer-support-chat)

definition.stemRaw: When presenting an architectural decision to a security and compliance reviewer, which set of content best aligns with that audience’s primary concerns?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Feature delivery schedule, roadmap dependencies, and scope boundaries for the product manager.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Implementation timeline, component interfaces, and deployment sequence for the engineering team.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Threat model, control mappings, residual-risk acceptance criteria, and audit traceability.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Decision rationale, business outcomes, and high-level risk summary for executive review.

definition.explanation: Security and compliance review focuses on identified threats, mappings from requirements to controls, the criteria for accepting residual risk, and traceable evidence for audits. These artifacts demonstrate that the architecture addresses security obligations and can be assessed for compliance.

definition.stemRaw:
You are addressing a stakeholder request that adds significant scope to a deployment already underway.  
  
Which response best aligns expectations while respecting the stakeholder’s underlying need?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Hide the scope-addition request from the broader delivery team to avoid a difficult conversation, allowing the change to proceed without team awareness of its timeline implications.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Decline the request outright without acknowledging the stakeholder’s underlying need or offering alternatives such as deferral, descoping, or timeline extension.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Acknowledge the request, describe the scope and timeline implications transparently, and propose options—defer it, descope something else, or extend the timeline—for the stakeholder to choose.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Accept the additional scope into the current release without describing the timeline or descoping implications, allowing the delivery plan to absorb unacknowledged changes until they surface as delays.

definition.explanation: Effective scope management makes the delivery and timeline effects of added work explicit, while preserving the stakeholder’s underlying objective through clear alternatives such as deferring the request, removing other scope, or extending the schedule.

definition.stemRaw:
You are preparing an operational runbook for a service based on Claude.  
  
Which content is essential to include in the runbook?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Dashboard and log references only, without alert definitions, triage steps, escalation paths, or rollback procedures for the on-call engineer to act on.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Common alerts and their triage steps, escalation paths, rollback procedures, and references to the relevant dashboards and logs.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Alert definitions and triage steps only, without escalation paths, rollback procedures, or references to dashboards and logs for on-call use.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Escalation paths and rollback procedures only, without alert definitions, triage steps, or dashboard references to guide initial incident response.

definition.explanation:
An effective runbook gives on-call engineers actionable procedures for common alerts, including triage and investigation guidance, escalation paths, recovery or rollback procedures, and links to the dashboards and logs needed to diagnose the service. AWS operational guidance likewise calls for a process per alert and defined escalation paths in runbooks and playbooks.

**Learn more:** [Responding to events - AWS Well-Architected Operational Excellence Pillar](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/operational-excellence-pillar/responding-to-events.html) · [Define escalation paths - AWS Well-Architected Framework](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/2023-04-10/framework/ops_event_response_define_escalation_paths.html)

definition.stemRaw:
You are assisting an engineer whose Claude Code session shows a permission denial when the engineer expected the action to be permitted.  
  
Which resolution step is most appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Tell the engineer to retry the denied action verbatim repeatedly until the denial stops appearing, without inspecting the active permission rules to determine whether the denial is intentional.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Disable the permission system entirely across all scopes to remove the denial, eliminating all tool-pattern and deny-rule controls rather than identifying and amending the specific rule.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Inspect the active permission rules across all scopes—managed, command-line, local, project, and user—to identify which rule is denying the action and confirm whether it should be amended or remain denied.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Grant the engineer unrestricted Bash access to bypass the specific rule causing the denial, removing all tool-pattern constraints rather than amending only the rule in question.

definition.explanation:
Claude Code exposes permission rules and the `settings.json` file from which each rule originates. Its deny rules are evaluated before ask and allow rules, while settings can be supplied at managed, command-line, project-local, shared-project, and user scopes. Inspecting the active rules and their source identifies whether a specific denial is intentional or whether the narrowly scoped rule should be amended, without removing unrelated safeguards.

**Learn more:** [Configure permissions - Claude Code Docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions) · [Settings files and precedence - Claude Code Docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings)

definition.stemRaw:
A technical team is deciding whether to implement a new capability that generates regulatory filings from internal data as a Claude Skill or an MCP server. The capability requires a fixed authoring procedure with embedded examples, does not need to invoke live external systems, and must be portable across three Claude deployments: claude.ai, an internal API integration, and Claude Code.  
  
Which factor most strongly supports implementing the capability as a Skill?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The capability needs to query a live database for the most recent regulatory filings.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The capability must also be callable from a developer’s command-line interface.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The capability requires direct authentication against the corporate identity provider.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The capability is procedural knowledge with no live external-system calls required.

definition.explanation:
Claude Skills are reusable packages of procedural knowledge, including workflows, instructions, resources, and examples, and custom Skills are supported in claude.ai, the Claude API, and Claude Code. MCP servers are designed to expose external systems such as data sources and tools. A fixed authoring workflow that has no live external-system calls is therefore best represented as a Skill.

**Learn more:** [Agent Skills — Claude Platform Docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/overview) · [What is the Model Context Protocol?](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/2026-07-28/getting-started/intro)

definition.stemRaw:
A customer-support team proposes assigning customer refund decisions to a Claude-driven workflow without human review for refunds below 50 USD. The team argues that small refunds are low risk and that human review would eliminate the efficiency benefit.  
  
Which Delegation-competency principle should guide your response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Delegation should always include human review on every decision the workflow produces.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Delegation scope should reflect the type of risk involved, not the transaction size alone.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Delegation scope should be set primarily by maximizing efficiency gains across the workflow.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Delegation should be avoided entirely wherever financial transactions occur in the workflow.

definition.explanation:
Delegation should be calibrated to the nature of the risk in the work being assigned. Financial refund decisions can carry fraud, policy-compliance, fairness, and customer-impact risks that are not determined solely by the refund amount; efficiency does not by itself justify fully autonomous approval. Anthropic’s Delegation guidance frames task allocation as a thoughtful distribution of work based on the task and the AI system’s capabilities and limitations.

**Learn more:** [Anthropic AI Fluency: Delegation](https://www.anthropic.com/ai-fluency/ai-fluency-delegation)

definition.stemRaw:
You are assembling guardrail tactics for a customer-facing assistant.  
  
Which two tactics should be included on the guardrail list?  
  
Each correct answer provides a complete solution.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Embed approved override phrases that let trusted users relax guardrails on demand.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lower sampling temperature globally to reduce the chance of off-policy completions.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Validate the model output against a structured schema before downstream actions are taken.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Layer prompt-level guardrails with runtime content checks rather than relying on either alone.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Rely on a single hardened system prompt that enumerates every disallowed behavior.

definition.explanation:
Validating output against a structured schema before downstream actions constrains the data that those actions can receive. Effective AI safety also uses defense in depth: prompt-level guidance must be supplemented by runtime content checks, because no single prompt or control provides sufficient protection on its own.

**Learn more:** [A Practical Guide to Building AI Agents](https://openai.com/business/guides-and-resources/a-practical-guide-to-building-ai-agents/) · [OpenAI Chat Completions API Reference](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/chat/object)

definition.stemRaw:
You are planning a feedback session for a deployment that is in progress.  
  
Which structure most effectively supports productive stakeholder feedback?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Hold an open-ended meeting with no pre-distributed agenda or artifacts, and rely on participants’ memory to carry decisions and follow-up owners forward.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Define a focused agenda, share the artifacts in advance, capture decisions and follow-ups in writing, and confirm action owners and dates.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Distribute artifacts at the session start rather than in advance, so stakeholders review materials in real time without preparation before the discussion begins.

choices.label: D
choices.text: End the session without recording decisions, follow-up items, action owners, or dates, relying on participant memory to carry the session’s outcomes forward.

definition.explanation: A focused agenda and advance distribution of artifacts let stakeholders prepare meaningful input. Recording decisions and follow-up actions, then confirming owners and due dates, creates shared accountability and ensures feedback is acted on.

definition.stemRaw:
A senior architect is developing briefing materials for a new retrieval architecture. The executive sponsor has asked for a summary of the architectural decision.  
  
Which framing is most suitable for that audience?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Technical alternatives evaluated, implementation implications, and component-level consequences.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Business outcomes achieved, trade-offs accepted, and high-level risks acknowledged.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Capabilities delivered, scope implications, and feature-level dependencies on the roadmap.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Threat model, control mappings, residual-risk acceptance, and audit traceability.

definition.explanation: Executive-level architectural communication should focus on the business outcomes enabled by the decision, the significant trade-offs involved, and the high-level risks that require awareness or sponsorship.

definition.stemRaw:
You are setting up Claude Code for a team that requires every engineer to use the same MCP server set, permission rules, and project context throughout the engineering monorepo.  
  
Which configuration scope best meets this requirement?
definition.explanation: Project scope stores repository-level configuration that can be version-controlled and shared with all collaborators. User and local scopes are personal or machine-specific, so they cannot reliably enforce a common MCP server set, permissions, and project context across a team.

definition.stemRaw:
You are conducting a discovery session with a business sponsor who requests “an AI system to fix our customer escalations.”  
  
Which approach is most likely to produce actionable requirements?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Accept the sponsor’s original phrasing as a complete and final requirement and proceed directly to design without asking targeted questions to surface actors, triggers, or constraints.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Decompose the request by asking targeted questions about who escalates, what triggers escalation, what good resolution looks like, and which constraints—latency, cost, audit, and data sensitivity—apply.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Defer the discovery session indefinitely on the grounds that the sponsor must fully specify the system before the architect can ask any clarifying or scoping questions.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Assume the requirement matches the architect’s previous engagement in a different industry and proceed with that context, without validating actors, triggers, or constraints for this sponsor.

definition.explanation: Actionable requirements require clarifying the people involved, the events that initiate escalation, the desired definition of successful resolution, and applicable nonfunctional constraints such as latency, cost, auditability, and data sensitivity. These details turn a vague solution request into scoping and design requirements.

definition.stemRaw:
You are incorporating AI-assisted tools into the team’s documentation workflow. The team wants generated documentation to remain grounded in the actual code.  
  
Which integration approach best meets this requirement?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Generate documentation from the model’s training-data recall without reading any of the actual repository code, accepting that the output will not reflect the current implementation.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Have the subagents publish generated documentation directly to the public-facing site without passing through the team’s normal review workflow or any human approval step.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Configure subagents that read the relevant code files via filesystem and code-search tools, generate the documentation, and emit changes through the team’s normal review workflow.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Disable all filesystem and code-search tools so the subagents cannot read any repository code, accepting that documentation generation will be entirely disconnected from the actual implementation.

definition.explanation:
Grounded documentation requires agents to inspect the relevant repository code through filesystem and code-search tools, so the content reflects the current implementation. Routing generated changes through the normal review workflow preserves human oversight and the team’s established quality controls.

**Learn more:** [OpenAI Codex CLI – Getting Started](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/11096431) · [Review pull requests with Codex](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001552-review-pull-requests-with-codex)

definition.stemRaw:
You are assembling team-setup practices for a Claude Code rollout across an engineering organization.  
  
Which two practices should be included on the list? Each correct answer provides a complete solution. (Select two.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use project scope for team-shared Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers and permission rules under version control.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Apply managed configuration centrally for security-critical settings that must not be overridden by individual engineers.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Use local scope for security-critical permission rules so each engineer can adapt them to ongoing work.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Use user scope for team-shared MCP servers so every engineer on the team has consistent access.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Use project scope for personal editor preferences so the preferences apply consistently within the project.

definition.explanation:
Project-scoped MCP servers are stored in `.mcp.json` and committed to version control so teammates receive the same tools. Shared project settings can likewise provide team permission rules. Managed settings are the appropriate scope for security and compliance requirements because they take precedence over personal, project, and local settings and cannot be overridden by individual engineers.

**Learn more:** [Claude Code MCP installation scopes](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp) · [Claude Code settings files and precedence](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings)

definition.stemRaw:
You are determining the highest-impact optimization for a deployment whose token cost is dominated by a long, recurring system prompt and a large retrieved context for each request.  
  
Which optimization most directly addresses the dominant cost driver?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Increase retrieval depth on every request to maximize recall, worsening the dominant cost driver by adding more retrieved tokens per request rather than reducing them.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Add additional repeated content to the system prompt to give the model more guidance.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Move the long, repeated system prompt into a cacheable prefix and trim retrieved context to the spans relevant to each query.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Switch every request to the heaviest available model to maximize output quality, accepting that higher per-request inference cost compounds rather than addresses the dominant cost driver.

definition.explanation:
Caching a stable, repeated prompt prefix allows its input tokens to be billed at the lower cached-input rate where supported, and restricting retrieval to query-relevant spans reduces the number of input tokens sent on each request. Together, these measures directly reduce the repeated-prompt and retrieved-context costs.

**Learn more:** [OpenAI API Pricing](https://platform.openai.com/pricing/) · [OpenAI Chat Completions API Reference](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/chat/object)

definition.stemRaw:
You are reviewing a peer's draft system prompt containing conflicting instructions: one section says never to speculate beyond the supplied source, while another instructs the model to confidently fill in any gaps.  
  
Which response is most appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Add a priority instruction directing the model to evaluate all instructions and apply whichever appears most contextually appropriate on each request.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Remove or rewrite the gap-filling instruction so the prompt consistently constrains the model to source-supported content.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increase temperature so output randomness masks the contradiction.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Keep both instructions and rely on the model to decide which one to follow on each request.

definition.explanation: System prompts should give consistent, unambiguous instructions. Removing or rewriting the instruction to fill gaps ensures the model does not invent unsupported information and remains constrained to content supported by the supplied source.

definition.stemRaw:
You are assessing an evaluation set used to score a Claude-based hiring-support tool. The set comes from a single geographic region and a single tenure band.  
  
Which response is most appropriate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Discard all quantitative evaluation and replace it with qualitative impressions collected from a small, convenience-selected group that may not represent the tool’s full user population.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Expand the evaluation set to cover the geographic regions and tenure bands the tool will serve, and rescore the system on the expanded set before broader release.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Reduce the evaluation set further to a single demographic subgroup to simplify score interpretation, narrowing coverage rather than expanding it to match the intended user population.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Continue using the narrow evaluation set drawn from one region and one tenure band because the existing benchmark scores are already high on that subset.

definition.explanation:
An evaluation set should represent the relevant population and the conditions in which the system will be deployed. Testing only one region and one tenure band cannot establish reliable or equitable performance for the broader hiring population; expanding the set and rescoring before wider release provides evidence across the intended coverage.

**Learn more:** [NIST AI Risk Management Framework Core and Profiles](https://airc.nist.gov/airmf-resources/airmf/5-sec-core/) · [NIST AI RMF Playbook](https://airc.nist.gov/docs/AI_RMF_Playbook.pdf)

definition.stemRaw:
You are conducting a controlled experiment to compare two prompts and must finish the design steps before running the experiment.  
  
Which two steps must be completed **BEFORE** running the experiment with random assignment? Each correct answer presents part of the solution. *(Select two.)*

choices.label: A
choices.text: Determine the minimum detectable effect size and the sample size needed for power.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Decide whether to promote, reject, or iterate the candidate based on the analysis.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Define the hypothesis and the primary success metric for the comparison.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Analyze the results against the predefined success metric and significance threshold.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Document the recommendation, the trade-offs accepted, and the alternatives considered.

definition.explanation:
A valid experiment is designed before assignment by defining the hypothesis and primary success metric, then planning statistical power. The minimum detectable effect and required sample size determine whether the experiment can reliably detect a meaningful difference. Result analysis, release decisions, and documentation occur after data has been collected.

**Learn more:** [Identify a hypothesis and determine success metrics for an experiment](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/commerce/experimentation-identify) · [Power Analysis](https://docs.statsig.com/experiments/power-analysis)

definition.stemRaw:
You are assessing a Claude-based deployment for compliance with a particular regulation.  
  
Which two steps must be performed **before** mapping the deployment’s data flows to individual regulatory clauses? Each correct answer represents part of the solution. *(Select two.)*

choices.label: A
choices.text: Compare the in-place controls against the regulatory requirements to identify any compliance gaps.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Identify the applicability of the regulation based on data types, jurisdiction, and audience.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Schedule the remediation work with the engineering team based on the prioritized gap findings.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Document the identified gaps along with recommended remediations and residual risk for sign-off.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Inventory the vendor-provided compliance tooling and confirm which compliance affordances are in place.

definition.explanation: Regulatory applicability must be established from the data types, jurisdiction, and audience before clause-level analysis can be scoped. The vendor’s available compliance tooling and enabled compliance affordances must also be identified so the actual controls and data-handling capabilities can be mapped to the applicable clauses. Gap analysis, remediation planning, and sign-off follow that mapping.

definition.stemRaw:
You are an architect supporting the iteration phase of a deployed Claude-based system.  
  
Which activity most directly aligns with this phase?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Rebuild the entire system architecture from scratch at the start of every iteration cycle regardless of what production telemetry, evaluations, and stakeholder feedback indicate is needed.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Stop measuring production outcomes once the deployment has successfully launched, treating the go-live milestone as the end of the evaluation and iteration cycle.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Discard the evaluation framework and reference set once the deployment is in production, accepting that future iterations will have no structured basis for measuring the impact of changes.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Review production telemetry, sampled output evaluations, and stakeholder feedback to identify the highest-impact change for the next cycle, then plan the change against the evaluation framework.

definition.explanation:
A deployed LLM system should retain its evaluation framework and use operational telemetry, sampled output quality, and user or stakeholder feedback to prioritize the most valuable improvement. The planned change can then be measured against defined success criteria and the established evaluation set, enabling evidence-based iteration.

**Learn more:** [Define success criteria and build evaluations — Claude Platform Docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/test-and-evaluate/develop-tests)

definition.stemRaw:
You are conducting a discovery engagement for a new Claude-based capability and must complete the requirements-gathering activities before validating the captured requirements with stakeholders.  
  
Which two steps must be completed **BEFORE** validating the captured requirements with stakeholders? Each correct answer presents part of the solution. *(Select two.)*

choices.label: A
choices.text: Produce architecture decision records that capture the rationale for major design choices.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Capture the business goals, success criteria, and the in-scope user population for the engagement.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Document the consolidated requirements with traceability to the source stakeholder for each item.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Schedule the rollout milestones and dependencies with engineering and product partners.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Identify the non-functional constraints covering latency, cost, audit, data sensitivity, and regulatory needs.

definition.explanation:
Business goals, measurable success criteria, scope, and the intended user population define the outcome the capability must serve. Non-functional constraints such as latency, cost, auditability, data sensitivity, and regulatory obligations bound which solutions are acceptable. These inputs must be elicited before stakeholders can meaningfully validate the requirements.

**Learn more:** [Define success criteria and build evaluations](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/test-and-evaluate/develop-tests) · [Claude prompting best practices](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-prompting-best-practices)

definition.stemRaw:
You are setting up tool permissions for a Claude-based assistant. Its defined duties require read access to a knowledge base and write access to a draft queue, with no other access.  
  
Which scoping design best enforces least privilege?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Allow access to all tools with read permissions globally and restrict write permissions to the draft-queue tool, without scoping to only the specific tools required for defined tasks.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Per-role allow-list of exactly the read-knowledge-base and write-draft-queue tools, enforced at the orchestration layer.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Allow access to every tool in the catalog and rely on the model to decline tools it should not use.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Disable all tools entirely to achieve a minimal permission surface, accepting that the assistant can no longer perform the read-knowledge-base or write-draft-queue tasks it was designed for.

definition.explanation: Least privilege requires granting only the specific capabilities needed to perform the defined duties. A per-role allow-list that permits only the knowledge-base read tool and the draft-queue write tool, enforced by the orchestration layer, prevents access to unrelated tools while retaining the required functionality.

definition.stemRaw:
The compliance team has developed a regulatory-disclosure procedure that must be used identically across customer-service, sales, and onboarding workflows. Regulators update the procedure four to six times per year. You are designing how to package the procedure for Claude’s use across all three workflows.  
  
Which two design decisions should you make? Each correct answer represents part of the solution. (Select two.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Package the procedure as a Claude Skill owned directly by the compliance team.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Embed the procedure text into each workflow’s system prompt at integration time.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Store the procedure in a shared retrieval corpus accessed by all three workflows.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Have each workflow team rewrite the procedure for its own context.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reference the same Claude Skill from all three workflow integrations.

definition.explanation:
A compliance-owned Claude Skill centralizes the approved procedure as a reusable, governed workflow. Referencing that same Skill from all three integrations keeps the customer-service, sales, and onboarding implementations aligned and lets compliance updates propagate from one maintained source. Anthropic documents Skills as a way to distribute approved, standardized workflows consistently, including organization-wide management and updates.

**Learn more:** [What are skills? | Claude Help Center](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12512176-what-are-skills) · [Use skills in Claude | Claude Help Center](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12512180-use-skills-in-claude)

definition.stemRaw:
A senior architect is overseeing stakeholder expectations for a Claude-based reporting assistant midway through development. Stakeholders have growing concerns about response latency.  
  
Which two actions most directly align stakeholder expectations in this situation? (Select two.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Present measured p50 and p95 latency baselines against the agreed SLA thresholds so stakeholders have accurate data.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Pause all development and reallocate engineering resources entirely to latency optimization.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Communicate that latency concerns are a known LLM limitation and outside the architecture team’s control.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Replace the current Claude model with a third-party model that may offer lower latency without evaluation.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Revise the SLA definition collaboratively with stakeholders if current targets are not achievable given production constraints.

definition.explanation:
Measured p50 and p95 latency compared with agreed SLA thresholds provides an objective, shared view of actual performance. If production constraints make the current targets unattainable, collaboratively revising the SLA realigns the service commitment with feasible performance expectations. Latency is a standard service-level indicator that may be evaluated using percentiles, and published service objectives set user expectations.

**Learn more:** [Google SRE Book — Service Level Objectives](https://sre.google/sre-book/service-level-objectives/) · [Anthropic Claude Platform Docs — Reducing latency](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/test-and-evaluate/strengthen-guardrails/reduce-latency)

definition.stemRaw:
You are deciding when to introduce a project subagent instead of relying on Claude Code’s general capabilities.  
  
Which scenario most directly warrants a dedicated subagent?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The team has a recurring specialized task, such as database schema review, that requires a focused system prompt, narrow tool permissions, and a specific model selection across many sessions.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The team has a one-time ad hoc question that will not recur and does not require a focused system prompt, narrow tool permissions, or dedicated model selection.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The team has no recurring specialized tasks and uses Claude Code only for isolated general-purpose work that does not justify a dedicated system prompt or tool scope.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The team wants every Claude Code interaction to use the same generic system prompt with no task-specific specialization, narrow tool permissions, or dedicated model selection.

definition.explanation:
A dedicated subagent is appropriate for recurring specialist work that needs a tightly scoped system prompt, restricted tool permissions, and optionally a distinct model. Custom Claude Code subagents are reusable and can be configured with their own system prompt, tool access, and model.

**Learn more:** [Create custom subagents - Claude Code Docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents) · [How and when to use subagents in Claude Code](https://claude.com/resources/articles/subagents-in-claude-code)

definition.stemRaw:
You are creating a human-in-the-loop validation workflow for a new Claude-based deployment and must finish the design steps before running a pilot of the workflow.  
  
Which two steps must be completed **BEFORE** piloting the workflow using a representative subset of traffic? Each correct answer represents part of the solution. *(Select two.)*

choices.label: A
choices.text: Define the sampling strategy and the escalation criteria at each oversight point in the pipeline.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Iterate the workflow design based on observed pilot findings before broader rollout to production.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Onboard the reviewer pool with role-specific training on the check criteria and escalation procedures.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Document the workflow with check criteria, escalation paths, and service-level agreements (SLAs) for each step.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Identify the decision points in the pipeline that require human oversight by impact and reversibility.

definition.explanation: A human-in-the-loop validation design must identify the pipeline decisions that warrant human oversight according to their impact and reversibility, and define the sampling and escalation criteria for each oversight point. Those controls establish the scope and behavior to be tested in the pilot; revisions based on pilot findings occur afterward.

definition.stemRaw:
Engineering leadership plans to deploy Claude Skills to 280 developers across 14 teams. The Skills will capture internal coding standards, code-review checklists, and incident-postmortem templates. Leadership has asked how Skill authorship should be governed so that Skills stay trustworthy without creating a bottleneck around one central team.  
  
Which governance model should you recommend?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Per-developer authorship across the 280 engineers with no team-level coordination required.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Centralized authorship by a single platform team responsible for every Skill produced.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Fully decentralized authorship across the 14 teams with no review before publication.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Federated authorship across the 14 teams with a central review and publication gate.

definition.explanation: Federated authorship enables each team to create and maintain Skills for its own domain, distributing the authoring workload. A central review and publication gate ensures that shared Skills meet organization-wide quality, security, consistency, and trust requirements before they become broadly available.

definition.stemRaw:
You are assembling continuity practices that extend across the deployment lifecycle.  
  
Which two practices should be included on the list? Each correct answer provides a complete solution. (Select two.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Maintain a stakeholder register and notify the listed parties at every phase transition event.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Carry the evaluation framework and reference set forward across iterations rather than rebuilding each time.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Archive every phase deliverable in long-term storage to preserve a record of what was produced.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Capture lessons learned at the end of each phase and surface them as inputs to the next phase.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Lock decisions made in early phases to prevent revisiting them as later phases begin.

definition.explanation:
A continuous deployment lifecycle uses a persistent evaluation framework and reference set so results remain comparable across iterations and regressions can be detected. It also incorporates lessons learned from each phase into the next phase, enabling systematic improvement. Microsoft guidance describes continuously operationalized evaluation and recommends postmortems to capture deployment lessons.

**Learn more:** [Build an iterative evaluation framework in four stages](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/agents/agent-evaluation/evaluation-iterative-framework) · [Architecture strategies for safe deployment practices](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/well-architected/operational-excellence/safe-deployments)

definition.stemRaw:
A Claude architect is reviewing configuration-scope assignments.  
  
Which two statements correctly describe an appropriate use of user-scope configuration versus other scopes? (Select two.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Persisting personal editor theme preferences that follow an engineer across projects.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Saving a preferred Claude response language that applies to all repositories the engineer uses.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Enforcing a company-wide policy that disables a feature for all engineers.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Defining MCP server endpoints shared by all contributors to a specific repository.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Storing API authentication keys so they are not committed to version control.

definition.explanation:
User-scope settings apply to one person across every project on that person’s machine and are intended for personal preferences such as a theme. A personal preferred response language used across all repositories therefore belongs at user scope. Organization-wide restrictions require managed settings, shared repository MCP endpoints require shared project configuration, and credentials should remain in private, uncommitted local configuration.

**Learn more:** [Claude Code settings files and precedence](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings)

definition.stemRaw:
You are choosing the documentation set that should accompany a Claude-based deployment at handoff.  
  
Which set is the most complete?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Architecture overview, ADRs, component-level diagrams, runbooks for common operations, an on-call playbook, and a list of known limitations.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Code comments scattered across individual source files with no integrating architecture overview, no ADRs, no runbooks, and no on-call playbook to orient operators or new team members.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A single one-page architecture diagram with no ADRs, no runbooks, no on-call playbook, and no list of known limitations to support operators or future maintainers.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A verbal handover walkthrough conducted on the day of transition, with no written architecture overview, ADRs, runbooks, playbook, or known limitations captured for future reference.

definition.explanation: A complete deployment handoff package documents the overall architecture and component design, records architectural decisions, provides runbooks for routine operations and an on-call playbook for support, and identifies known limitations for operators and future maintainers.

definition.stemRaw:
A security audit identifies two issues:  
  
1. All end users use one shared API key.  
2. Tool calls run without logging the user who initiated them.  
  
Which two mitigations directly remediate these specific findings? (Select two.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Validate structured outputs against a schema before downstream actions are executed.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Enforce RBAC at the retrieval layer before content enters the model context.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Move credentials out of the prompt context and resolve them from a server-side secret store.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Add actor attribution to tool-call logs so each call records the initiating user identity.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Replace the shared API key with per-user OAuth tokens carrying scope-restricted permissions.

definition.explanation: Per-user OAuth tokens replace a shared credential with individually attributable, scope-limited access. Including the initiating user’s identity in tool-call logs establishes accountability and an audit trail for each action.

definition.stemRaw:
You are categorizing token-management tactics by the request-lifecycle stage at which each applies.  
  
For each tactic, select its applicable request-lifecycle stage.

blanks.label: Persist the validated output for downstream consumption and audit.
Order the prompt sections so cacheable content sits before per-request content.
Summarize prior conversation history when full history is no longer needed.
Validate the model's structured output against the expected schema.
Move stable repeated content into a cacheable prefix at the head of the prompt.
Trim retrieved passages to spans relevant to the user's question.

definition.explanation:
Input preparation reduces or condenses conversation and retrieved context before it is assembled. Prompt construction determines the ordering and stable cacheable prefix of the prompt. Output handling validates generated structured data and persists validated results for downstream use and auditing.

**Learn more:** [Prompt caching](https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/prompt-caching) · [Structured Outputs](https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/structured-outputs)

definition.stemRaw:
You are addressing an adversarial input pattern where users insert text that claims administrative authority and directs the model to circumvent safety restrictions.  
  
Which combination of controls most effectively mitigates this attack pattern?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Trusting that the model will intrinsically recognize and reject all bypass attempts without prompt-level instructions, runtime classifiers, scoped permissions, or audit logging.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Prompt-level instructions that treat user content as untrusted data, runtime classifiers that detect override attempts, scoped tool permissions that cannot be elevated by user content, and audit logging of attempts.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Removing all safety restrictions and guardrails to eliminate the attack surface that bypass attempts target, accepting that this makes the assistant unrestricted for all inputs.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Granting users any privilege level they assert in their message content, on the assumption that cooperative behavior requires honoring self-declared authority without independent verification.

definition.explanation: User-provided text must be treated as untrusted and cannot confer privileges or override higher-priority safety rules. Layered mitigations—prompt instructions, runtime detection of override attempts, least-privilege tool permissions that user content cannot elevate, and audit logging—reduce both the likelihood and impact of prompt-injection attempts.

definition.stemRaw: When the support agent invokes escalate_to_human, human agents report they must re-read the entire raw conversation to understand each case, and average handle time for escalated tickets has risen. What should the agent do at the moment of escalation to fix this?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Attach the full untrimmed transcript of the conversation so the human has complete information.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Enable extended thinking on the escalation turn so the model reasons longer before handing off.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Escalate earlier in ambiguous cases so humans receive tickets before much conversation has accumulated.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Produce a structured handoff summary — the customer's issue, verified identifiers, tool results and account state gathered, actions already attempted, and the specific recommended next step.

definition.explanation: Why D is correct. Effective human handoff requires a structured summary that front-loads exactly what the human needs: the problem, confirmed identifiers, what was tried, and a recommendation. That is what removes the re-reading burden and shortens handle time. Dumping the full transcript (A) is the current failure mode — it forces the human to reconstruct the case themselves. Extended thinking (B) improves the model's own reasoning but produces no artifact for the human. Escalating earlier (C) changes when tickets arrive, not the missing information problem, and would likely lower first-contact resolution.

definition.stemRaw:
You are evaluating two configurations for an internal compliance Q&A assistant. Configuration X decreases top-k retrieval and uses a lighter model, reducing p95 latency by 38 percent but resulting in a measured 2 percent decrease in the accuracy benchmark. Configuration Y keeps the current top-k retrieval setting and heavier model, with no change to p95 latency and no measurable accuracy change. The deployment’s declared priorities are accuracy first and latency second.  
  
Which configuration is the better recommendation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Configuration X, because the 2 percent accuracy reduction falls within normal benchmark variance and is not a meaningful regression.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Configuration Y, because the deployment’s stated priority is accuracy first, and Configuration X produces a measured reduction in accuracy.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Configuration X, because lower latency generally matters more than accuracy, regardless of the deployment’s stated priorities.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Configuration X, because a 38 percent latency improvement outweighs a 2 percent accuracy reduction as a general rule across compliance deployments.

definition.explanation: When accuracy is the primary deployment priority, the configuration that maintains measured accuracy is preferable. Configuration Y preserves accuracy, while Configuration X introduces a measured accuracy regression; its latency improvement is secondary to that stated priority.
